title: triage-beads documents three bd commands that error out when run
description:
## Why (Computational)

`skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md` tells an agent to run three commands that `bd` rejects. An agent
following the skill hits an error and has no documented recovery, so the triage readout stops.

All three verified by running them against the installed `bd` on 2026-08-31:

```
$ bd blocked --json --limit 0
Error: unknown flag: --limit

$ bd list --status=closed -a --limit 3 --json --sort updated_at
Error: bd list does not accept positional arguments; use flags instead

$ bd list --status=draft --limit 1
Error: invalid status "draft" (valid: open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, closed, pinned, hooked)
```

Sites:

- `bd blocked --json --limit 0` at two places: the Step 1 fetch block, and the Command reference
  table. `bd blocked` has no `--limit` flag at all.
- `bd list --status=closed -a --limit 50 --json --sort updated_at` at two places: the momentum
  signal gathering, and the Command reference table. Two faults in one line. `-a` is
  `--assignee string` and takes a value, so it swallows `--limit`, and `50` then falls through as
  a positional argument. Separately, `updated_at` is not a valid sort field; the valid set is
  priority, created, updated, closed, status, id, title, type, assignee.
- `draft` is used as a status in three places: a rule saying `bd ready` excludes it, an
  exclusion-table row, and a footer count line. `bd` has no `draft` status. `bd ready --help`
  says it excludes in_progress, blocked, deferred, and hooked. So the row and the count are dead,
  and an agent testing for `draft` finds nothing forever.

Two further factual errors about defaults, same file:

- The skill says `bd ready` defaults to 20. It defaults to 100.
- The skill says `--limit` defaults to 50 for `bd list`, `bd ready`, and `bd blocked`. That holds
  for `bd list` only.

These all pre-date tadw-7xq.2, which only reworded the file. Found by a fresh-eyes review of that
change on 2026-08-31.

## Estimated size

1 file, about 15 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Replace each broken invocation with one that runs:

- `bd blocked --json --limit 0` becomes `bd blocked --json`.
- `bd list --status=closed -a --limit 50 --json --sort updated_at` becomes
  `bd list --status=closed --limit 50 --json --sort updated`. Keep the trailing note that
  `--reverse` flips the order; that is correct once the field name is fixed.
- Replace the `draft` status with `hooked`, or delete the rule, the exclusion-table row, and the
  footer count together. Decide which by checking whether this repository ever uses `hooked`.
- Correct the two default-limit claims.

Run every command in the file against the live `bd` before closing. That is what found these.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given every bd command written in skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md, when each is run against the
   installed bd, then each exits 0.
2. Given the skill's statements about default limits, when compared to `bd list --help`,
   `bd ready --help`, and `bd blocked --help`, then each statement matches the tool.
3. Given the word "draft" in the file, when searched, then it either does not appear as a status
   value, or it has been replaced by a status bd accepts.
4. Given rumdl fmt --check . and check_doc_paths.py, when run, then both pass.
notes: Found by /tadw:fresh-eyes-cr during tadw-7xq.2 on 2026-08-31. All defects pre-date that bead, which was a rewording pass only. Priority P1 because these are the only findings that make the skill fail outright at runtime rather than merely mislead.
close_reason: shipped: fix: correct three bd commands triage-beads documents (tadw-pdi)

title: Bead-label hook: resolve real branch shapes, and stop dirtying the tree
description:
The bead-labeling hook resolves no bead from an outrigger branch, so a full build-and-ship session on 2026-08-22 in ~/Dev/fathom labeled nothing across three skills.

Two defects, landed together because either alone is worse than both.

1. resolve_bead's candidate regex is [a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)+(\.[0-9]+)*. The + on the hyphen group makes at least one hyphen mandatory, and the leading [a-z] rejects a digit. Reproduced 2026-08-22: branch outrigger/zkc.5/rank-beads-and-reminders-deterministical yields exactly one candidate, the slug, and bd show rejects it. Every short bead id in fathom is hyphen-free, so the hook is blind to every outrigger branch there.

2. refresh_export runs bd export after every successful label, which leaves the tracked tree modified. outrigger's pre-flight and /tadw:ship Step 4 both refuse a dirty tree, and both hit it in that same session while the hook was labeling nothing. Fixing (1) alone converts an intermittent collision into one that fires on every review pass.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M1 and M2. Cite by function name, never by line number (plan section 0).
design:
M1: resolve_bead builds candidates from three ordered sources. Positional first (segment two of a branch with three or more slash-separated segments, which is outrigger's outrigger/<short-id>/<slug>), then the widened pattern [a-z0-9][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*(\.[0-9]+)*, then a cap of 12 unique candidates longest-first. Verified: the widened pattern emits outrigger, zkc.5, and the slug against the real branch.

M2: refresh_export skips the export unless the export file is already modified, or TADW_BEAD_LABEL_EXPORT=1 is set. bv reads the database directly, so it costs bv nothing; the env var covers Manifest, whose reader is unconfirmed.

M2 inverts a committed test that asserts the opposite, so the test change ships in the same commit or the pre-push hook blocks the push.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Branch outrigger/zkc.5/rank-beads-and-reminders-deterministical resolves to the bead whose short id is zkc.5. This is the regression case for the whole outage.
2. Branch feature/tadw-alpha-one/x still resolves, so the widened pattern breaks nothing the seven existing add_branch cases cover.
3. Branch main resolves nothing, returns non-zero, and logs.
4. A branch whose slug alone matches a real bead resolves the positional segment first, not the slug.
5. A branch offering more than twelve candidate tokens issues at most twelve bd show probes, asserted against recorded argv.
6. On a clean tree, a labeled skill runs bd update and no bd export. This replaces label/bd: refreshes the export instead of committing it, which asserts the opposite.
7. With TADW_BEAD_LABEL_EXPORT=1, the export runs.
8. With .beads/issues.jsonl already modified, the export runs without the env var.
9. After case 6, git status --porcelain is empty.
10. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
close_reason: Implemented on branch outrigger/tadw-b14/hook-resolution-and-visibility; 173 checks pass and each fix was observed to fail against the pre-fix script

title: Sanitize git env vars in the pre-push hook before running checks
description:
## Why (Computational)

git runs the pre-push hook with GIT_DIR exported. From the main checkout the value is the relative path .git, so a fixture-building test that runs git -C <tmpdir> init resolves it under the tmpdir and stays isolated. From a linked worktree (.claude/worktrees/...) the value is an absolute path, -C does not redirect it, and the fixture's git init re-initializes the MAIN repository's gitdir as bare. Observed on 2026-08-14: a push from a linked worktree left the main .git/config with core.bare=true and core.excludesFile=/dev/null (the latter written by test_changed_set.py's fixture at skills/quality-gates/scripts/test_changed_set.py:116), which broke every work-tree git operation in both checkouts until repaired by hand. The corrupting suites are test_changed_set.py, test_check_secrets.py, and test_check_hygiene.py, all of which build git fixtures and all of which the pre-push hook runs.

The stakeholder is anyone who pushes from a Claude Code worktree, which is how agent sessions push.

## Fix sketch

Unset GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, and GIT_PREFIX at the top of .githooks/pre-push before any check runs (the hook's cwd is the worktree root, so git re-discovers correctly). Belt and suspenders: the fixture helpers in the three test scripts can also pass env={...} scrubbed of GIT_* to subprocess.run, so running a suite directly under any GIT_DIR is safe too.

## Estimated size

2-4 files, about 20 LOC, band: Target.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e5517a: the pre-push hook unsets the six GIT_* variables before its first git call, the three fixture suites clear the same names at import, and test_prepush.py gained a linked-worktree case that fails without the hook change

title: Give the .claude/scripts hooks a test harness
description:
## Why (Computational)

The three hooks in `.claude/scripts/` have no automated coverage, and they are the most dangerous
code in this repository: `autocommit_beads_after_br.sh` (since deleted) and `label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh`
both ran `git commit` and `git push` to main, and `close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh` closes a bead and
pushes. `hooks/test-hooks.js` covers the style-core hooks only, so nothing here tests these.

That gap is not theoretical. A fresh-eyes pass over commit 9ce0f8a found six defects across the
three scripts, and f8259ea fixed all six with manual verification and no pinned tests. Two of the
six were guards that read as active and never fired, which is exactly the class a test catches and
a reading does not:

- `close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh` matched bead ids with `[a-z]+-[a-z0-9]{2,8}`, which extracts
  `tadw-qg` from `tadw-qg-script-secrets-gate-jbg`. The hook could never close a bead here, and it
  had shipped that way.
- Its `status == "unknown"` guard never fired, because `bd show <missing-id> --json` writes to
  stderr and leaves stdout empty, so `|| echo unknown` produced the empty string instead.

The stakeholder is anyone who trusts these hooks to move tracker state. A silently inert hook
means beads stay open and someone closes them by hand without knowing why.

## Estimated size

2 files, about 300 LOC, band: Stretch.

Stretch is justified because a harness with no cases is not a harness. The fake `bd`, `git`, and
`gh` on PATH are the load-bearing part, and they only prove themselves against real cases.
design:
One `hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh` (or a Node peer of `hooks/test-hooks.js`, if that
reads better beside the existing suite), plus a registration line in the AGENTS.md command block.

The load-bearing design decision is how to run a hook that shells out to `bd`, `git`, `gh`, and
`jq` without touching the real tracker or the real remote. Three rules:

1. FAKE THE TOOLS ON PATH, do not mock inside the scripts. Each case builds a temp dir holding
   executable `bd`, `git`, and `gh` stubs, then prepends it to PATH. The scripts stay unmodified,
   so the test exercises the shipped code rather than a test-only branch. A stub records the
   argv it received to a file, which is how a case asserts what the hook tried to do.
2. NEVER let a case reach the network or the real repo. `git push` in a stub is a no-op that
   records. A case that would push asserts against the recording, not against a remote.
3. FEED REAL PAYLOAD SHAPES on stdin. The hooks read a Claude Code hook payload, so a case
   passes the same JSON shape the runtime sends: `hook_event_name`, `tool_input.command`,
   `tool_input.skill`, `tool_response.stderr`.

Assert on three observable things, in this order of value: the exit status (always 0, since every
failure path is designed to let the session continue), the recorded argv of `bd` and `git`, and
the stderr log lines.

Pin the six f8259ea fixes specifically. Each case should fail when its fix is reverted, and the
bead is not done until that has been checked per case rather than assumed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the harness, when it runs with no `bd`, `git`, or `gh` on the real PATH beyond its own stubs, then every case passes and no case reaches a network or the real .beads database.
2. Given a payload whose command is `bd update x --claim && bd show x`, when the autocommit hook runs, then the recorded argv shows it reached the commit path, and reverting the subcommand-detection fix makes that case fail.
3. Given a payload whose command is `bd show x`, when the autocommit hook runs, then no `git commit` is recorded.
4. Given a merged PR whose title names `tadw-qg-script-secrets-gate-jbg`, when the close hook runs, then the recorded argv closes that full id, and reverting the id-regex fix makes the case fail.
5. Given a merged PR whose body names two real beads and carries no `Bead:` trailer, when the close hook runs, then no `bd update --status=closed` is recorded and the log says it refused.
6. Given a merged PR whose body carries a `Bead: <id>` trailer that disagrees with the title, when the close hook runs, then the trailer id is the one closed.
7. Given a `bd show` stub that prints its error to stderr and nothing to stdout, when the close hook runs, then no close is recorded, and reverting the empty-status guard makes the case fail.
8. Given a worktree checkout on main, when either the close hook or the label hook runs, then the recorded argv reaches the canonical tracker. (Retired 2026-08-21: `bd` takes no `--db` pin, so the worktree cases now assert that no call carries one.)
9. Given a gate-mode marker named `<label>__<id>` for a label other than `qa-d`, when the Stop handler runs against a passing report, then that label is applied and not `qa-d`.
10. Given every case, when the suite finishes, then it prints a real pass and fail count and exits non-zero on any failure.
11. Given AGENTS.md, when reading "Commands for This Repo", then the harness appears there and its path resolves on disk.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A single command runs the whole harness, and it is listed in the AGENTS.md command block
- The three hooks are unmodified by this bead: the harness fakes tools on PATH rather than adding
  a test-only branch to shipped code
- No case touches the real `.beads` database, the real git remote, or the network
- Each of the six f8259ea fixes has a case that was OBSERVED to fail with the fix reverted, not
  assumed to. Record the observation in the commit message the way f8259ea recorded its manual runs
- The suite reports real counts and exits non-zero on failure

## Out of scope

- The `gate` mode QA-report path beyond criterion 9. Gate mode is dormant in this repository,
  because it reads `.gstack/qa-reports/` and `/qa` is a gstack skill. Criterion 9 covers the label
  plumbing, which is the part f8259ea changed. Full report-parsing coverage is a separate bead if
  gstack is ever installed here.
- A pre-push hook that runs this harness. That belongs to tadw-qg-prepush-hook-suites-w8r, which
  already owns the AGENTS.md command list as its input.

## Provenance

Filed after `/verify-acceptance` graded commit f8259ea INCONCLUSIVE for the hook half, on the
ground that no bead recorded what those three scripts had to achieve. The criteria above were
written from the defects found, so treat them as regression coverage rather than as a
specification the fixes were built against.

## Amended 2026-08-21 (tracker cutover)

The tool name above is now `bd`; the earlier CLI is gone from this repository. Two criteria lost
their subject with it and are retired rather than met:

- Criteria 2 and 3 tested `autocommit_beads_after_br.sh`, which was deleted. It existed only
  because that tracker wrote its state into a git-tracked export; `bd` writes to a gitignored
  database, so there is nothing to auto-commit.
- Criterion 8 tested the `--db` pin, which `bd` does not take. The worktree cases that replaced it
  assert the same guarantee from the other side: a hook run from a worktree still reaches the
  canonical tracker, and no call carries a `--db`.

The suite is now 60 checks, down from 63.
close_reason: hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh: 63 checks over 22 cases, registered in AGENTS.md and .githooks/pre-push. All 8 fixes observed to fail against a reverted copy. Deviation recorded: git is real behind a recording stub rather than fully faked, because a git reimplementation would be the wrong subject under test.

title: Add a pre-push hook that runs the repository's checks
description:
## Why (Computational)

`AGENTS.md` lists nine commands under "Commands for This Repo", and running them is a
convention, not a mechanism. The only hard gate in this repository is
`.githooks/reference-transaction`, which fires on `v*` tags alone, so commits and pushes ride
entirely on the session remembering.

The stakeholder is the author who pushes a broken formatter or a failing suite and finds out
late, or never.

Author direction, recorded as D4 in the plan: enforcement is a local git hook, not GitHub
Actions. `.github/workflows/lint.yml` keeps the checks it runs today and gains nothing new.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M2)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
One POSIX sh `.githooks/pre-push`, modeled on the existing
`reference-transaction` hook, running the `AGENTS.md` command list minus `evals/run.py`.

Three deliberate behaviors carry the design:

1. Run every check even after one fails, then report all failures together. A hook that stops at
   the first failure makes the author push, fail, fix, push, fail again.
2. A missing tool warns and allows, naming the tool. This follows the precedent
   `reference-transaction` set for a missing `claude`: an unpushable clone is worse than an
   unchecked push, and `rumdl` and `node` are not universally installed.
3. `TADW_PREPUSH=off` is a documented escape rather than an undocumented workaround, documented
   the way `TADW_STYLE_CORE=off` already is.

`evals/run.py` is excluded because each case is a real model call, far too slow and too expensive
to sit on a push.

A push that only deletes refs has nothing to check, so allow it. Keep output quiet on success:
one summary line, not ten.

`AGENTS.md` has a "Release gate (one-time setup per clone)" section documenting
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Broaden it to cover both hooks rather than adding a second
setup section, since one `core.hooksPath` call now serves both.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a throwaway clone with `core.hooksPath` set and a badly formatted markdown file, when `git push --dry-run` runs, then the push is refused and the output names that file.
2. Given `TADW_PREPUSH=off` in the environment, when the same push runs, then it proceeds.
3. Given `rumdl` absent from PATH, when the push runs, then it proceeds and the output names `rumdl` as skipped.
4. Given two failing checks, when the push runs, then both failures appear in the output.
5. Given the diff against the base, when inspecting `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, then it is unchanged.
6. Given a push that only deletes a remote ref, when the hook runs, then it allows the push without running the suites.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `.githooks/pre-push` exists, is executable, and is POSIX sh
- Breaking one file's formatting makes a push fail and names that file
- `TADW_PREPUSH=off` lets the same push through
- A missing tool warns by name and allows
- Two simultaneous failures both appear; the hook does not stop at the first
- `AGENTS.md` documents both hooks under one setup section
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` is unchanged
- The hook's wall time is measured and stated in the `AGENTS.md` section

## Out of scope

The verdict-gating stage. That is the "Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict" bead, which
appends a second stage to this same file.
close_reason: done

title: Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict
description:
## Why (Computational)

A session can run the gates, get a FAIL, and push anyway, leaving no trace and
hitting no barrier. "Landing the Plane" in `AGENTS.md` tells the session to run the gates before
pushing, but nothing checks that it did, or what it found.

The stakeholder is the author's future self, and anyone who pulls a commit that its own QA said
was not fit to ship.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M4)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 70 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Append a second stage to the `.githooks/pre-push` file the suite-running bead
created. Git calls exactly one `pre-push` hook, so two responsibilities on the same event must
share a file with separate stages.

Read `quality-gates-report.json` from `$(git rev-parse --git-dir)` through `python3 -c`; do not
parse JSON in sh, and do not hardcode `.git/`. The writing skill resolves the same way, and the
reason is worktrees: `--git-dir` returns a distinct path per linked worktree, so each worktree's
hook reads that worktree's own verdict. A literal `.git/` is a file rather than a directory inside
a worktree, and `--git-common-dir` would let every worktree overwrite the others' verdict.
Verified 2026-08-11 with a three-worktree probe: a pre-push hook run from each worktree resolved
its own git dir and read its own planted report.

The forgiveness rules are the design, not an afterthought:

- No report, or an unreadable report, warns and allows. Absence is not evidence of a problem, and
  blocking there would make the hook unusable for documentation pushes and teach people to
  disable it.
- Only a recorded verdict of FAIL blocks. The message names the verdict, the recorded head, and
  the timestamp, plus both exits: re-run `/quality-gates`, or set `TADW_PREPUSH=off`.
- A verdict whose recorded head is not an ancestor of the pushed commit warns as stale, using
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, but still allows.

Then add one line to `AGENTS.md` "Landing the Plane" step 4 noting the refusal.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a `.git/quality-gates-report.json` with verdict FAIL, when `git push --dry-run` runs in a throwaway clone, then the push is refused and the output names the verdict, the head, and the timestamp.
2. Given no report file, when the push runs, then it proceeds and prints exactly one warning line.
3. Given a report whose recorded head is not an ancestor of the pushed commit, when the push runs, then it proceeds and prints a staleness warning.
4. Given a report with verdict PASS whose head is current, when the push runs, then it proceeds silently.
5. Given the repository, when `node hooks/test-hooks.js` runs, then it passes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A hand-written FAIL report refuses a dry-run push in a throwaway clone
- `TADW_PREPUSH=off` lets that push through
- No report file means one warning line and a successful push
- Both stages live in one `.githooks/pre-push` and report separately
- `AGENTS.md` "Landing the Plane" step 4 notes the refusal
- `node hooks/test-hooks.js` still passes
close_reason: Stage 2 of .githooks/pre-push reads the recorded verdict and refuses a FAIL. 30 checks in test_prepush.py, all criteria graded ACCEPTED.

title: Fix the command/skill namespace collision in all 18 commands that delegate with 'load the skill'
description:
A command file and a skill directory that share a name also share one `tadw:` invocation namespace, and the command wins. When such a command's body says "Use the `<name>` skill", invoking it returns the command body, whose first line redirects to itself, so the skill is never loaded.

This is not theoretical. `/bead-audit-all` shipped this way and every backlog sweep it ran scored from a twenty-line summary instead of the 661-line rubric, reporting confident numbers computed from nothing. A wrong number produced this way is indistinguishable downstream from a right one, which is what makes the class dangerous rather than merely untidy.

18 commands collide by name, and the triage below shows all 18 delegate. `/bead-audit-all` is not one of them: no `skills/bead-audit-all/` exists, so it never collided. Its 2.4.1 fix is the pattern to copy, not a reduction of the work.

## Triage result (completed 2026-08-09)

All 18 colliding commands delegate by name. **Zero are self-contained.** An earlier read of this bead assumed body length was a proxy for safety; it is not. Commands with 10 to 20 lines of their own instructions still open with "Use the `<name>` skill", so they redirect exactly like the one-line ones.

Total skill content unreachable by name: **271,067 bytes.**

| Command | Skill bytes shadowed |
|---|---|
| /bead-audit | 51,113 |
| /plan-to-beads | 31,438 |
| /ux-audit-ios | 22,598 |
| /product-surface-docs | 18,979 |
| /ux-audit | 18,291 |
| /plan-review | 16,858 |
| /ab-test-design | 13,614 |
| /product-roadmap | 12,830 |
| /product-research | 12,492 |
| /research-ingest | 12,193 |
| /agentic-clean-code | 11,288 |
| /competitive-analysis | 10,702 |
| /product-brief | 9,257 |
| /aso-audit | 8,933 |
| /verify-acceptance | 8,314 |
| /roadmap-dashboard | 7,596 |
| /business-ideas | 2,740 |
| /idea-wizard | 1,831 |

Classification test used: the command body matches `(use|load|invoke) the \`?<name>\`? skill` and contains no `SKILL.md` read. Reproduce it by re-running that match over `commands/` against the `skills/` directory names.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `/bead-audit` on any bead, in a session with the plugin loaded.
2. Watch which file the Skill tool returns. It is `commands/bead-audit.md` (20 lines), not `skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md` (661 lines).
3. Confirm the substitution directly: the returned body carries the resolved `$ARGUMENTS` value, which only a command receives.

Expected: the audit rubric loads. Actual: the command body loads and redirects to itself.

The 18 colliding names, from `comm -12` over `commands/` and `skills/`: ab-test-design, agentic-clean-code, aso-audit, bead-audit, business-ideas, competitive-analysis, idea-wizard, plan-review, plan-to-beads, product-brief, product-research, product-roadmap, product-surface-docs, research-ingest, roadmap-dashboard, ux-audit, ux-audit-ios, verify-acceptance.

## Why the runtime does this

`claude plugin details tadw` reports 72 registered skills for 35 skill directories and 37 commands. Commands and skills occupy one namespace, and each colliding name holds two entries. The cost table shows both, for example `plan-review ~50 always-on ~6.2k on-invoke` (the skill) beside `plan-review ~50 always-on ~330 on-invoke` (the command). The command's description is the one surfaced to the model.
design:
Three fixes exist, and the choice is per command. The triage is done, so every one of the 18 needs one of them.

**A. Read the skill from disk.** Replace the delegating line with an explicit `Read` of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, plus a `Glob` fallback and an assertion that named headings are present in the file that was read. This is what `/response-style` and `/bead-audit-all` do. Keeps the command name. Costs a hardcoded path per command, forever, and the pattern must be remembered for every command written afterward.

**C. Delete the command and let the skill take the name.** Verified empirically on 2026-08-09: `commands/competitive-analysis.md` was moved out of the installed plugin, the registered skill count fell from 72 to 71, the surviving entry kept the skill's on-invoke cost (~3.9k, not the command's ~0.1k), and after a restart the slash menu showed the skill's own description ("Deep competitor teardown with positioning map, moat analysis, feature gaps..."). The file was restored and the plugin re-validated at exit 0.

Nothing is lost that matters. `$ARGUMENTS` still works, since four skills already use it. Only `argument-hint` is lost, which is a menu display hint rather than behavior. Deleting also repairs the agents: `agents/product-manager.md` tells itself to load these same skills by name and hits the identical dead end today.

**B. Rename one side.** Give the command a distinct name so no collision exists. This is what 19 of the 37 commands already do (`/fresh-eyes-cr` for `review-fresh-eyes`, `/prod-ops` for `production-ops`). Breaks any hardcoded invocation path in other repos.

**Recommended: C for any command whose content is skill content, A for any command that carries genuine per-invocation instructions worth keeping under a slash name.** C is preferred by default because it removes the collision rather than working around it, and costs nothing afterward.

The governing rule to encode: **a command may share a skill's name, or delegate to that skill by name, but never both.**

Sequence. Fix `/bead-audit` first, since 2.4.1 ships a README callout telling users to avoid it. For each remaining command, decide C or A by asking whether the body says anything that is not already the skill's job; most of it (for example `/ux-audit` naming the `ux-product-designer` role) reads like skill content and should move into the skill before the command is deleted.

Guard against regression with a check in `hooks/test-hooks.js`, which already asserts that `/response-style` reads its skill file rather than invoking it. Generalize that check to every colliding name.

3. MET, 2026-08-09, after installing 2.5.0 and restarting. The menu shows the skill's own description for bead-audit ("against the Marr audit, size audit, type-specific section audit, and a grounding audit against the current main branch") rather than the deleted command's ("against the Marr, size, and type-specific section standards"). Verified by resolution rather than by grepping the loaded body; the description comes from the skill's frontmatter, so the file being read is the skill.
4. MET. Check 18 in hooks/test-hooks.js. Proven to discriminate, not merely to pass: injecting a delegate-by-name regression into /ux-audit exits 1 naming that command; removing only its Glob fallback exits 1 naming that; restoring leaves the file byte-identical and the suite green.

The second clause does not, and it was wrong when written. It assumed every collision would be eliminated; the chosen design keeps 10 commands that share a name and read from disk, so those 10 names register twice on purpose. Amended clause: no name may appear twice unless its command reads the skill from disk, which check 18 enforces.
6. MET. The /bead-audit callout in README.md now says the command file was removed and the skill takes the slash name. AGENTS.md carries the namespace rule instead of the "only /bead-audit-all has been fixed" wording.
7. MET. rumdl fmt --check . clean over 106 files; 19 hook checks pass with the docs/HOOKS.md count verified; claude plugin validate . exits 0; 25 framework-leak checks pass.

Not done when the 18 are merely surveyed. The survey is finished; the edits are the deliverable.

Option C (delete the command, let the skill take the name) was verified empirically on 2026-08-09 by moving commands/competitive-analysis.md out of the installed plugin and restarting. Details in the Design field.

title: Check path claims inside skills, commands, and agents
description:
## Why (Computational)

check_doc_paths.py builds its document list from README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/**,
so it never opens skills/, commands/, or agents/. Those files carry the delegation paths every
command depends on. A typo in one breaks the command with no error message, and Gate 5 reports
a clean run.

A trial run over the three directories found 20 path claims that do not resolve, of which two
are genuinely misleading.

Found by /quality-gates while building tadw-x8b.5.

## Estimated size

5 files, 60 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Extend resolve_docs in skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py to add
skills/*/SKILL.md, commands/*.md, and agents/*.md to the default document list.

The 20 misses that surface fall into three groups, and each needs a different answer:

- Output directories a skill creates at run time (docs/product/, docs/experiments/). These are
  the same class as docs/ux-audits/*, already in .docpaths-ignore. Add them there.
- The file-name table in agents/claude-md-reviewer.md, which recommends target files for the
  repository being reviewed rather than naming files here. Add those names to .docpaths-ignore
  with that reason.
- commands/bead-audit.md, named in commands/bead-audit-all.md to explain why it was deleted.
  Same class as agents/quality-gates.md, already ignored. Add it, permanently.

Two misses are real, and the fix is in the document rather than the ignore file.
commands/roadmap-dashboard.md and agents/product-cartographer.md both write a script path that
is relative to a skill directory, and the repository root holds a different scripts/ directory.
Write the repo-rooted path in both.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a command whose delegation path does not resolve, when check_doc_paths.py runs with no
   arguments, then it reports that command and exits 1.
2. Given the current tree, when check_doc_paths.py runs with no arguments, then it exits 0 and
   reports a document count above 90.
3. Given the repository, when python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/test_check_doc_paths.py runs,
   then every check passes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The default document list covers skills/*/SKILL.md, commands/*.md, and agents/*.md.
- Every ignore-file entry added carries a reason beside it.
- The two misleading script paths name their real location.
- check_doc_paths.py exits 0 on the current tree.
- test_check_doc_paths.py covers the widened document list.

## Out of scope

Widening the checker to references/ files under a skill directory.

title: Check the README command rows the way the skill rows are checked
description:
## Why (Computational)

hooks/test-hooks.js:536 asserts that README.md documents every component on disk, but its loop
iterates only Skills and Agents. A command added without a README row passes every check in this
repository, so the table a person reads to find a command drifts silently from the directory.

Found by /quality-gates while building tadw-x8b.5, which added /research-synthesize.

## Estimated size

1 file, 20 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add Commands to the loop's label list at hooks/test-hooks.js:540.

The names differ in shape between the directory and the README, so the check cannot compare them
directly. componentNames returns a command as research-synthesize, and README.md writes it as
/research-synthesize. Give the COMPONENTS entries the prefix the README uses, and build the
search string from it, so one loop serves all three lists.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a command file on disk with no README row, when node hooks/test-hooks.js runs, then it
   fails and names that command.
2. Given the current tree, when node hooks/test-hooks.js runs, then every check passes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The README check iterates Skills, Agents, and Commands.
- The command lookup matches the leading slash the README writes.
- The suite still passes on the current tree.

title: Register the new research components in the plugin
description:
## Why (Computational)

/validate-plugin checks the CLAUDE.md name lists against the directories on disk, so an
unregistered skill fails validation and never appears in the README.md tables a person reads to
find it. The repository's own rule is that adding a component means editing two places.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 6.

## Estimated size

3 files, 25 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add research-synthesize to the CLAUDE.md skill list and /research-synthesize to the command
list, and update both counts, which read 45 and 31 before this change.

Add rows to the README.md command table and skill table, and refresh the agent row for the
extended librarian role.

Update the routing-gap sentence in CLAUDE.md, which lists the commands that have no
docs/ROUTING.md entry yet.

Then run the four validator seams the plan names.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the registration edits are made, when /validate-plugin runs, then it reports no
   unregistered component.
2. Given the registration edits are made, when rumdl fmt --check ., claude plugin validate .,
   and check_doc_paths.py run, then all three exit 0.
3. Given README.md is read, when the command table is scanned, then /research-synthesize has a
   description row.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The CLAUDE.md skill and command lists include the new names, and both counts match the
  directories on disk.
- Both README.md tables carry a row for the new component.
- All four seam commands exit 0.

## Discovered while building tadw-x8b.5, 2026-08-31

hooks/test-hooks.js asserts that the AGENTS.md name lists match the component directories on
disk. A branch that adds a skill or a command without registering it fails that suite, so

title: Answer research questions across the wiki
description:
## Why (Computational)

Nothing ever reads the Research wiki except the next ingest, so the owner still has to re-read
the sources to answer a question. This is the missing half of the Karpathy LLM Wiki pattern the
pipeline was built from, and it is what turns the archive into a brain.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 5.

## Estimated size

3 files, 225 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add skills/research-synthesize/SKILL.md and commands/research-synthesize.md.

The command Reads the skill file rather than invoking it, because a command and a skill sharing
a name share the tadw: invocation namespace and the command wins. Copy the pattern already
documented in commands/research-ingest.md lines 8 to 10.

The skill finds candidate pages through the index, the aliases, and Grep, reads the source
summaries behind them, weights each claim by the page's validity and verification frontmatter,
then writes a question page at Research/wiki/questions/<Question>.md.

The question page requires a confidence field and a "What Would Change This Answer" section, so
a thin wiki cannot produce an answer that reads as authoritative.

Contradiction handling reuses the ingest skill's existing callout protocol rather than inventing
a second one.

Extend agents/research-librarian.md so its description covers synthesis as well as ingest, per
the plan's proposed answer to its Open Question 3.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given /research-synthesize "does X cause Y", when it completes, then a question page exists
   with Evidence For and Evidence Against sections, each entry citing a source page and its
   validity.
2. Given a question page is written, when it is read, then Research/questions.md links it.
3. Given /research-synthesize with no argument, when it runs, then the open items in
   Research/questions.md are offered for selection, and none is answered until one is picked.
4. Given two sources disagree, when the question page is written, then both appear, one under
   Evidence For and one under Evidence Against.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Both new files exist, and the command Reads the skill rather than invoking it.
- The question page schema carries status, confidence, sources_for, and sources_against.
- The skill states how validity and verification weight a claim.
- The no-argument mode reads Research/questions.md and offers its open items.
- The agent description covers synthesis.

## Out of scope

Registering the new skill and command in CLAUDE.md and README.md. That is the sibling bead for
milestone 6.

Appending each ingest's Open Questions to Research/questions.md. That is the sibling bead for
the agenda harvest.
