title: Make the ingest write Obsidian-native pages
description:
## Why (Computational)

Pages carry no aliases field, so a page named Large Language Models never captures a link
written as [[LLM]], and the graph fragments into synonym islands the owner cannot navigate. The
hand-written Stats block in Research/index.md is a count the skill cannot keep true, and a stale
count looks exactly like a fresh one.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 4.

## Estimated size

1 file, 60 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Three edits across Steps 4 to 6 of the ingest skill.

Populate aliases at page creation. Tell the writer to check existing pages' aliases before
creating a page, so a synonym updates the existing page instead of creating a second one.

Create or update a MOC page, meaning a Map of Content hub page that lists a theme's pages, once
a theme reaches eight pages.

Delete the Stats block from the Step 6 index instructions. The index stays hand-maintained until
the plan's Open Question 1 settles which Obsidian plugin the vault runs, so this work is not
blocked on that answer.

Update the Quality Checklist rows to match the new instructions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a new concept page, when it is created, then its frontmatter carries aliases, and no
   second page exists for a name an existing page already lists as an alias.
2. Given a theme reaching eight pages, when an ingest touches that theme, then a MOC page for it
   is created or updated.
3. Given an ingest completes, when Research/index.md is read, then it holds no hand-written
   count.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Every entity and concept page schema carries an aliases field.
- Step 5 tells the writer to check aliases before creating a page.
- The MOC rule names its eight-page threshold.
- The Stats block is gone from the Step 6 instructions.
- The Quality Checklist rows match the new instructions.

## Out of scope

Replacing the index body with an Obsidian Bases view or a Dataview query. That waits on the
plan's Open Question 1.

title: Ingest a batch of sources in one review conversation
description:
## Why (Computational)

The skill requires a blocking discussion per source, so ten new sources cost ten conversations.
That is the cost that makes a vault owner stop ingesting, and an unprocessed backlog is the
failure mode of every note system.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 3.

## Estimated size

2 files, 90 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Branch on the count of unprocessed sources in Step 1. For two or more, read and assess all of
them, write draft briefings and draft pages into Research/staging/, then hold one review
conversation over the whole batch using AskUserQuestion, which the agent already carries.

Promote drafts into Research/wiki/ only after that conversation, then update the index and the
log once for the batch.

The one-source path stays exactly as it is today, so current behavior is not disturbed. The
user-discussion principle survives because the wait happens once per batch, not zero times.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given three unprocessed sources, when /research-ingest runs, then the user is offered batch
   mode, drafts appear in Research/staging/, and exactly one review conversation happens before
   anything is written to Research/wiki/.
2. Given one unprocessed source, when /research-ingest runs, then the flow matches the current
   single-source behavior.
3. Given a batch the user has not yet reviewed, when the review conversation has not happened,
   then Research/wiki/ is unchanged.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Step 1 states the two-source trigger for batch mode.
- The staging flow names Research/staging/ and forbids promotion before the review conversation.
- The index and the log update once per batch.
- The single-source path is unchanged.

## Out of scope

Migrating any existing vault's pages. The new flow applies from the next ingest onward.

title: Verify a source against the web before its validity verdict
description:
## Why (Computational)

The validity rubric asks whether a source has been retracted or replicated, but
agents/research-librarian.md lists no WebSearch or WebFetch tool, so the answer comes from model
memory. A wiki that records a guess as a verification is worse than one that records nothing,
because a future reader cannot tell the two apart.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 2.

## Estimated size

2 files, 50 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add WebSearch and WebFetch to the agent's tools list.

Add Step 2c to the skill, capped at three lookups: resolve the DOI or canonical URL, search for
retractions and corrections, search for replications or contradicting work. The cap exists
because verification can expand without limit and the ingest must still finish.

Record the outcome in two new frontmatter fields, verification and verification_notes.

When the tools are unavailable, write verification: unverified and say so in the briefing. Never
block the ingest on a failed lookup.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a source with a DOI and working web tools, when Step 2c runs, then the source page
   records verification and verification_notes naming the retraction and replication checks.
2. Given no web access, when Step 2c runs, then the ingest completes with
   verification: unverified and the briefing says verification was skipped.
3. Given a source Step 2c found retracted, when the briefing is presented, then the retraction
   appears in the key caveats.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- agents/research-librarian.md lists WebSearch and WebFetch.
- Step 2c exists, names its three lookups, and states the three-lookup cap.
- The frontmatter schema carries verification and verification_notes.
- The no-web path is written as a completed ingest, not an error.

title: Adapt the ingest validity rubric to the source's genre
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 2b of skills/research-ingest/SKILL.md asks about blinding, randomization, and power
calculations for every source. For an ML paper, an essay, or a talk transcript, most of those
return "not applicable", and the questions that would catch a weak source of that genre go
unasked. Every ingest pays this cost, so it is the highest-frequency defect in the pipeline.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 1.

## Estimated size

1 file, 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add a genre detection step before the rubric, then a routing table to six short rubrics:
empirical study (the current list, unchanged), ML or CS paper, journalism, essay or opinion,
transcript or talk, and book chapter.

Cap each new rubric at five questions, to hold the file's size down. Every genre ends in the
unchanged Validity: verdict block, so pages stay comparable across genres.

Add genre to the source-page frontmatter schema.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given an ML paper as the source, when Step 2b runs, then the briefing asks about baselines
   and code release, and does not ask about blinding.
2. Given a clinical study as the source, when Step 2b runs, then the questions match the
   current rubric.
3. Given any genre, when Step 2b completes, then the output ends in the same Validity: verdict
   block.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Step 2b names six genres and routes to one rubric per genre.
- Each new rubric holds five questions or fewer.
- The Validity: block is identical across every genre path.
- The source-page frontmatter schema carries a genre field.

title: Turn the Research wiki into a working knowledge base
description:
## Why (Computational)

The vault owner's research pipeline only files knowledge; nothing reads it back, so the wiki is
an archive rather than a brain. Four frictions compound this: a clinical-trial validity rubric
applied to every genre, a verification question the agent has no tools to answer, one blocking
conversation per source, and a page shape that fragments the Obsidian graph into synonym islands.

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md

## Success Criteria

- The vault owner can ask the wiki a question and get an answer weighted by source quality,
  without reading the sources again.
- A backlog of unprocessed sources clears in one sitting instead of one conversation per source.
- Two pages for the same concept under different names stop appearing.
design:
Keep the two-half shape. The ingest half stays as edits to skills/research-ingest/SKILL.md and
agents/research-librarian.md. The synthesis half mirrors it as a new skill and a new command.

The halves meet in the page frontmatter: ingest writes validity and verification, and synthesis
weights each claim by them.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A source of any genre gets a rubric that fits it, and still ends in the same Validity: block.
- A question can be asked of the wiki and produces a question page citing sources for and against.
- Ten new sources cost one review conversation, not ten.

title: Record a live verify-app run against a real application
description:
## Why (Computational)

Every other bead in this plan proves structure: the files parse, the paths resolve, the skill loads.
None proves the technique works. A verification skill that has never verified anything is exactly the
guessing this plan set out to replace.

## Estimated size

2 files, 60 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Fill a control document for one real project, drive two journeys, and record both transcripts in this
bead. Run one journey that works and one with a known defect, because a verification that cannot fail
is not a verification. Fix whatever the runs expose in skills/verify-app/SKILL.md rather than working
around it in the control document.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a real running application, when `/verify-app` drives a working journey, then it ends with
   `VERIFY_PASS`.
2. Given the same application with a known defect, when `/verify-app` drives the broken journey, then
   it ends with `VERIFY_FAIL <step>` naming that step.
3. Given both transcripts, when a second person reads them, then they can tell which application was
   driven and which journey each transcript covers.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Both transcripts are in this bead, and each ends with `VERIFY_PASS` or `VERIFY_FAIL <step>`.
- The failing run names the step that broke and quotes the on-screen error text.
- Any correction the runs forced is committed to `skills/verify-app/SKILL.md`.

title: Route the quality-gates handoffs to verify-app
description:
## Why (Computational)

A change to a web page can be graded ACCEPTED today with nobody having opened the page.
`skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md` Step 4 runs three gates, and none of them is a handoff row, so
the INCOMPLETE that `quality-gates` recorded never reaches the verdict.

## Estimated size

2 files, 45 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Change two files. In skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md Step 3, point the browser-ui row at
tadw:verify-app and the mobile-ui row at tadw:verify-app-ios, and add the browser lane to the owner
table. In skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md, add HANDOFF to the verdict rules so an unresolved
handoff gives INCONCLUSIVE. Keep it INCONCLUSIVE rather than NOT ACCEPTED, because an unrun check
proves nothing about the code, matching how that skill already treats a BLOCKED gate.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a change that touches a web page, when `/quality-gates` runs, then the handoff row names
   `tadw:verify-app` and names no skill from another plugin.
2. Given a report holding an unresolved HANDOFF row, when `/verify-acceptance` runs, then the
   verdict is INCONCLUSIVE and the report says which handoff is unresolved.
3. Given a resolved handoff carrying `VERIFY_PASS`, when `/verify-acceptance` runs, then the handoff
   does not by itself make the verdict INCONCLUSIVE.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Both files name `tadw:verify-app`, and neither names `/qa` or `/ios-qa` as the owner of a row.
- The verdict rules in `skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md` list HANDOFF beside FAIL and BLOCKED.

title: Add the verify-app skill, agent, and command
description:
## Why (Computational)

Nothing in this plugin drives a running web application to prove a change works. The
`skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` Step 3 router hands a `browser-ui` change to `/qa`, which belongs to
another plugin, and marks the run INCOMPLETE. A person is the only thing that opens the page today.

## Estimated size

6 files, 495 LOC, band: Stretch. A skill, its agent, and its command are one registrable unit, and
`/validate-plugin` reports a finding whenever one of the three is missing. The comparable `ux-audit`
set runs 390, 38, and 24 lines.
design:
Write skills/verify-app/SKILL.md covering six steps: read the control document, load the browser
tool in one ToolSearch call, launch and poll until the application answers, reach a signed-in
session, drive the journey taking a snapshot before each screen, then report. Report a selector that
no longer matches as its own outcome, never as FAIL, because a moved selector is stale documentation
and not a defect. End with a machine-readable line, VERIFY_PASS or VERIFY_FAIL <step>, so
quality-gates can read a result it dispatched. Add agents/verify-app.md so the orchestrator can
dispatch it per ADR 0002, and commands/verify-app.md taking a journey name, nothing, or a sentence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a project with a control document and a leaf document carrying a drive block, when
   `/verify-app <journey>` runs, then it launches the application, drives the journey, and ends with
   `VERIFY_PASS` or `VERIFY_FAIL <step>`.
2. Given a journey whose success signal never appears, when `/verify-app` runs, then it reports
   FAIL, names the step that broke, and quotes the on-screen error text.
3. Given a drive block whose selector no longer matches the page, when `/verify-app` runs, then it
   reports a stale selector and does not report FAIL.
4. Given no browser tool enabled in the project, when `/verify-app` runs, then it stops and says
   which tool to enable.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `claude plugin validate .` exits 0.
- `/validate-plugin` reports no broken reference and no new orphan.
- The three registration places name the new component: `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and
  `docs/ROUTING.md`.
- The skill reports and never edits, stated in its Critical Rules.

## Out of scope

- The iOS surface, which is its own bead.
- Changing how `quality-gates` routes, which is its own bead.

title: Write the verification control document template
description:
## Why (Computational)

Every journey in one project shares the same launch command, the same sign-in path, and the same
browser tool. Repeating those in every leaf document makes them drift. The `verify-app` skill needs
one place to read them, and no such document exists in any project yet.

## Estimated size

1 file, 100 LOC, band: Target.
design: Write skills/verify-app/references/control-template.md holding six fields: launch, ready_check, base_url, auth, browser, and teardown. A project copies it to docs/verification/control.md and fills it once. Copy the split from ll:verify-commons, which keeps environment and authentication apart from the journey.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the template, when a person fills it for a project, then `verify-app` can start that
   application and reach a signed-in session without asking a question.
2. Given a project whose application needs no teardown, when the author fills `teardown`, then the
   template gives them a way to say so rather than leaving it empty.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The template holds all six fields, each with one line saying what goes in it and one filled
  example.
- The `auth` field says plainly not to click through a signup form when signing in is only setup.

title: Add a How to drive this section to the leaf document template
description:
## Why (Computational)

An agent that can launch an application still cannot find a feature in it. The leaf documents under
`docs/products/` describe what a feature is, never how to reach it. The `verify-app` skill needs the
route, the precondition, the selector, the action, and the success signal. No document holds them
today.

## Estimated size

1 file, 30 LOC, band: Target.
design: Add one section to the leaf template in skills/product-surface-docs/SKILL.md, beside the existing 'What is visible' section. Five named lines, one per field, so a checker can read the shape without parsing prose. Put it in the leaf template alone, because a surface document describes many features and cannot carry one route.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the leaf template, when a reader follows it, then the document produced holds Route,
   Precondition, Selector, Action, and Success signal.
2. Given a feature with no user interface, when an author follows the template, then the section
   says how to mark it as not drivable rather than leaving it blank.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The leaf template in `skills/product-surface-docs/SKILL.md` names all five lines: Route,
  Precondition, Selector, Action, Success signal.
- The section says what a leaf that nobody can drive, such as a background job, writes instead.

title: Check that every bd command documented in a fenced block actually runs
description:
## Why (Computational)

A skill can document a `bd` command that `bd` rejects, and nothing notices. An agent following the
skill hits an error mid-run and has no documented recovery.

This has happened twice. `tadw-pdi` fixed three such commands in `skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md`:

```
$ bd blocked --json --limit 0
Error: unknown flag: --limit

$ bd list --status=closed -a --limit 3 --json --sort updated_at
Error: bd list does not accept positional arguments; use flags instead

$ bd list --status=draft --limit 1
Error: invalid status "draft" (valid: open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, closed, pinned, hooked)
```

Both times a person found them, once by reading and once by a `/tadw:fresh-eyes-cr` pass. No check
in this repository runs a documented `bd` command, so a third occurrence would arrive the same way.

The repository already has the pattern to copy. `check_doc_paths.py` asserts that every path a
document names exists. This is the same check for commands instead of paths.

## Estimated size

2 new files, about 300 LOC total (script plus its test suite), and 2 edits to register it.
Band: Target.
design:
Write `skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_documented_bd_commands.py`, in the `check_doc_paths.py`
mold: a script with its own regression suite, not a prose method.

**Extract from fenced code blocks only.** This is measured, not assumed. Running both fenced blocks
and inline backticks over the doc tree on 2026-08-31 produced 29 candidates and 3 failures, and all
three were prose fragments rather than commands: `bd show`, `bd list --status`, and `bd search`.
Restricting to fenced blocks produced 17 candidates and 0 failures. A command in a fenced block is
meant to be run; a name in backticks is prose. This is the same false-positive trap that
`check_doc_paths.py` was written to escape, where its first run reported 194 missing paths and none
were real.

**Skip a candidate that cannot be run verbatim.** That means any command carrying a placeholder
(`<id>`, `{id}`, `$VAR`, `$(...)`), or a pipe. Report the skipped count so a reader can see what
was not checked.

**Run only a read-only safelist**: list, show, ready, blocked, stats, search, epic, prime, where,
doctor. Never run create, update, close, delete, import, export, or dolt. The script runs against
the real tracker, so a write would make a check that mutates what it checks.

**Exit codes**, matching the other scripts here:

- 0: every extracted command exits 0.
- 1: at least one failed. Report each with its `file:line`, the command, and bd's own first error
  line. Map this to FAIL rather than WARN, because a documented command that errors stops a run.
- 2: operator error, such as a root that is not a directory.

**A missing `bd` warns by name and exits 0.** CI has no `bd` and no tracker database, so blocking
there would refuse every push from CI. This matches the pre-push hook's existing policy for a
missing tool.

**Register it in two places**: the check list in `CLAUDE.md` under "Commands for This Repo", and
`.githooks/pre-push`. Both the script and its suite go in the list, so the count in that section's
prose moves from 12 to 14.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a Markdown file with a fenced block holding `bd blocked --json --limit 0`, when the script
   runs, then it exits 1 and names that file, that line, and bd's error text.
2. Given a Markdown file whose only bd mention is `bd show` inside inline backticks, when the script
   runs, then it exits 0, because prose is not a command.
3. Given a fenced block holding `bd update <id> --claim`, when the script runs, then it runs no
   command and counts the line as skipped, because it carries a placeholder and is a write.
4. Given the repository as it stands after tadw-pdi lands, when the script runs, then it exits 0.
5. Given a PATH with no `bd`, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and warns that it verified
   nothing.
6. Given `python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/test_check_documented_bd_commands.py`, when run,
   then it exits 0, and each acceptance criterion above has a case in it.
7. Given `.githooks/pre-push` and the check list in `CLAUDE.md`, when each is read, then both name
   the script and its test suite.
notes:
## Out of scope

Checking prose claims about bd's behavior, such as "`--limit` defaults to 50" or the set of
statuses `bd ready` excludes. Those need a marked claim and a `--help` comparison, which is a
different mechanism. `tadw-pdi` corrected six such claims by hand. Revisit only if a wrong number,
rather than a broken command, is what costs time next.

Checking `bv` commands. Same idea, different tool, and no `bv` defect has been seen yet.

## Provenance

Found by `/tadw:quality-gates` on 2026-08-31, grading tadw-pdi. That run graded change coverage FAIL
because the diff's seven cases were all claims about bd's command-line interface and nothing
committed re-checked any of them.

## Dependency

Depends on tadw-pdi. Until that lands, `skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md` on main still holds
`bd blocked --json --limit 0` in a fenced block, so criterion 4 cannot pass.
close_reason: Implemented check_documented_bd_commands.py with its 16-case suite; registered in AGENTS.md check list and .githooks/pre-push (12 to 14 checks); all acceptance criteria have passing cases

title: plan-to-beads and plan-review disagree on decomposing a plan with no acceptance criteria
description:
## Why (Computational)

These two skills run next to each other in pipeline A, and they give opposite instructions for the
same input.

**The cross-file contradiction.** `skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md` says that if the plan has no
acceptance criteria at all, say so, author them per bead from the plan's goals and scope, and
recommend the user run `/plan-review`. That is, decompose anyway. `skills/plan-review/SKILL.md`
says a plan without acceptance criteria cannot be decomposed into beads, fails the gate, scores
Actionability RED, returns Major Rework, and names `/plan-to-beads` only on a Ready verdict. One
document permits exactly what the other forbids.

**Within plan-to-beads:**

- It says "Epics carry no size estimate", while the body shape lists `## Estimated size` with no
  type tag, the Always list says to estimate size for every bead, the Step 3 example gives an epic
  a size of "2 / 90, Target", and the checklist asserts every bead falls in the Target or Stretch
  band. The epic create block is also the only one omitting the section.
- It says "the `→` annotations below say which native field each section belongs in". There are no
  `→` annotations; the template uses HTML comments. `## Out of scope (optional)` carries no
  annotation at all, though the Step 5 table routes it to `--notes`.
- The "task or feature" create block hardcodes `-t task`, so an agent following it files every
  feature as a task. The bug and epic blocks correctly use `-t bug` and `-t epic`.
- The partial-failure states cover "fully written", "created but unpopulated", and "never
  attempted", but the text says to stop if either `bd create` or its follow-up exits non-zero. A
  failed `bd create` fits none of the three states.
- It cites ADR 0001 for "`bd create` cannot set these fields, so creation takes two calls". ADR
  0001's own 2026-08-21 correction says `bd create` does accept `--design`, `--notes`, and
  `--acceptance`, and that whether this skill moves to a single call is an open decision. The
  two-call apparatus should be attributed to this skill's choice, not to the ADR.
- The size band vocabulary appears three ways: Trivial/Target/Stretch, that set plus "Too big",
  and a five-band table including "Hard ceiling". The audit tests for "Too big" or "Hard ceiling",
  which the canonical template cannot express.
- One line says every plan stage maps to a bead; everywhere else the unit is a milestone, and the
  canonical plan template has milestones and no stages.
- The checklist asserts unconditionally that every bead is Target or Stretch and that Trivial work
  was demoted to a direct commit, but the audit only fails a Trivial bead when it is also
  standalone. A Trivial bead with dependents is permitted by the audit and fails the checklist.

**Within plan-review:** three dimensions band the middle as a count of "1-2" with a qualitative
RED, so a plan with 5 thin-but-present sections, or 5 unverifiable claims, or 6 minor findings,
falls in no band. A plan missing `## Acceptance Criteria` also scores RED under both Completeness
and Actionability, which the file's own "single bucket per finding" rule forbids. The
acceptance-criteria-versus-success-metrics pairing has no branch for a plan that declares no
success metrics, though the neighboring roles pairing shows exactly that pattern.

All pre-date tadw-7xq.2, which only reworded these files.

## Estimated size

2 files, about 60 LOC, band: Stretch.
design: Settle the cross-file contradiction first, because the rest of plan-to-beads' behavior depends on it. Two options. A: plan-to-beads stops and routes to /plan-review when a plan has no acceptance criteria, which makes plan-review's gate real. B: plan-review drops the 'cannot be decomposed' claim and keeps the RED score as advice. Prefer A, because the gate exists to stop unbuildable beads from being created, and B leaves the gate with no consequence. Then fix the within-file defects, which are independent of each other.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a plan with no acceptance criteria, when plan-to-beads and plan-review are read together,
   then they give the same instruction.
2. Given an epic, when plan-to-beads is read, then the body shape, the Always list, the Step 3
   example, the create block, and the checklist agree on whether it carries a size estimate.
3. Given the template's field annotations, when the prose describes them, then it names the form
   the template actually uses, and every section carries one.
4. Given the create block for a task or a feature, when followed for a feature, then the bead is
   created with type feature.
5. Given a failed bd create, when Step 5b is consulted, then a state covers it.
6. Given the ADR 0001 citation, when checked against that ADR, then the citation matches what the
   ADR says.
7. Given each plan-review dimension, when any count of findings is supplied, then exactly one band
   matches.
8. Given a plan missing Acceptance Criteria, when scored, then exactly one dimension owns the
   finding.
notes: Found by /tadw:fresh-eyes-cr during tadw-7xq.2 on 2026-08-31, all pre-existing. Filed as one bead because the cross-file contradiction determines several of the within-file fixes; split it if the two files end up with separate owners.

title: bead-audit's verdict model and scorecard contradict each other in six places
description:
## Why (Computational)

`skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md` computes a three-state verdict and an optional 0-100 score, and
other components gate on both. Six internal contradictions make the result depend on which
paragraph the agent read last.

The seven worked scorecard examples were recomputed and all seven are correct, so the weights and
the denominators are sound. The defects are in the prose and the tables around them.

1. **The report template gives Estimated size a flat `n/a` structure cell**, but the structure
   term counts it. The "task, no Acceptance Criteria" example scores 78.0, which only works as
   content 70 plus structure `10 × 4/5 = 8`. That requires Size to be one of the 5 required
   sections. The cell should read `canonical / variant / absent`.
2. **"`score` is capped by verdict" is false, and self-refuting.** The rule is to compute the raw
   score, map it to a band, then take the lower of that band and the ceiling. The examples report
   raw 100.0 with band Adequate. Only the band is capped. The sentence also says the band may be
   lower than the score implies, which cannot happen if the score itself were capped.
3. **"Excellent is exactly equivalent to PASS" is false once grounding caps apply.** The examples
   report a PASS bead at raw 100.0 as Adequate when `drifted` and Weak when `satisfied`. Excellent
   implies PASS, not the reverse.
4. **The REFORMAT row for a Trivial size band is unsatisfiable as written.** It requires "all
   content `pass`" plus band Trivial, but band Trivial is itself defined as a content warn, and
   the matching example scores 95.0 = 20+20+20+20+5+10, that is, size content at half weight.
5. **Step 6 can never clear a bead whose only defect is a Trivial size band.** Step 6 requires
   every section at `content: pass`, and reformatting cannot turn a Trivial band into a pass. The
   bead carries no placeholder and is grounded, so `blocked_on` is empty and it is neither
   `applyable` nor routed to a human. The loop contract then cannot terminate.
6. **N/A size bands are given the verdict "Pass"**, while another rule says an N/A dimension has
   no pass/warn/fail and simply leaves the denominator. Read literally, "Pass" puts size back into
   the numerator and denominator, making an epic's denominator 100 instead of the documented 90.

Two smaller ones in the same family: the file calls a structure `variant` a "WARN" twice, though
`warn` is a content verdict worth half weight and the rollup vocabulary is PASS / REFORMAT /
NEEDS WORK; and the type-defaulting WARN belongs to no section, so it enters no verdict, no
score, and no JSON field.

Also, the inverse grounding check omits Success Criteria, and the JSON `section` enum has no
`success-criteria` value, so an epic can never be reported `satisfied`.

All pre-date tadw-7xq.2, which only reworded the file.

## Estimated size

1 file, about 30 LOC, band: Target.
design: Each fix is a wording correction to a rule or a table cell, not a change to the weights. Do not change any weight, denominator, or worked example: all seven were recomputed and are correct. Fix the prose to match them. For defect 5, add an explicit carve-out that a Trivial-band warn is a route-to-human finding rather than a draftable one, since reformatting cannot resolve it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the report template's Estimated size row, when read, then its Structure cell admits
   canonical, variant, or absent.
2. Given the sentence about capping, when read, then it says the band is capped and the score is
   not.
3. Given the claim about Excellent and PASS, when read, then it states the implication in one
   direction only, or names the no-ceiling condition.
4. Given the REFORMAT row for a Trivial band, when its condition is tested against the Trivial
   band's own verdict, then the condition is satisfiable.
5. Given a bead whose only defect is a Trivial size band, when Step 6 runs, then the loop
   terminates by routing it to a human.
6. Given an N/A size band, when the denominator is computed, then it is excluded, and the table
   says so rather than saying "Pass".
7. Given the seven worked scorecard examples, when each is recomputed after the change, then each
   still produces its printed value.
notes: Found by /tadw:fresh-eyes-cr during tadw-7xq.2 on 2026-08-31, all pre-existing. One reported finding was rejected as a false positive: the denominator formula is correct. The weight table totals 110, so task is 100 with Steps excluded, epic is 90 with Steps and Size excluded, and bug is 110, exactly as documented.

title: triage-beads scoring model has an undefined band, unordered overrides, and a wrong sample report
description:
## Why (Computational)

`skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md` turns a bead into a number, and two agents scoring the same bead
should get the same number. Six defects break that.

1. **The Med impact band has no rule.** The value table awards `User impact | High 4 · Med 2 ·
   Low 0`, but the rules below define only High and Low. Nothing says when a bead is Med. Two
   agents can differ by 2 points, which is the gap between the sample board's first and second
   rows.
2. **The two hard overrides can select different beads, with no precedence.** Rule 1 says an
   overdue ready bead "is the pick, whatever its score". Rule 2 says a ready P0 "outranks every
   non-P0, whatever the arithmetic". An overdue P2 beside a ready P0 satisfies both. Rule 1 also
   selects a set rather than one bead, and the four-key tiebreak is explicitly scoped to
   candidates that survive the overrides, so two overdue beads have no tiebreak.
3. **The sample report scores its top pick Hot on evidence the rules define as Warm.** The
   evidence line reads "13 open qg-hardening beads name the same plan file". A shared label and a
   shared plan file are both Warm. Hot requires a dependency edge whose other end just moved, and
   the same report says "0 in progress", so the second Hot clause cannot fire either. Corrected,
   value is 3 + 0 + 4 + 1 = 8, so ROI is 8.0 rather than the printed 9.0. That ties the pick with
   the second row, and the tiebreak then decides it on unblocks. The pick survives; the headline
   number does not.
4. **The S evidence in the sample contradicts the S rule.** The sample cites "4 acceptance
   criteria (S)". The inference rule defines S as one to three acceptance criteria.
5. **The sample report's counts do not add up.** It says "7 of 12 ready". The rows show 1 pick
   plus 3 leaderboard rows plus 2 tail rows plus "and 5 more", which is 11 of 12. The leaderboard
   cap is 5, so a fifth leaderboard row is most likely missing.
6. **The divisor rationale cites a value range its own examples contradict.** It says value spans
   about 3 to 8 points on a typical backlog. The file's own worked example uses 15 and 9, and the
   sample board uses 9, 8, 11, and 4. Three of six exceed 8. The sizing argument for a 1 / 1.5 /
   2.5 divisor rests on that range.

All six pre-date tadw-7xq.2, which only reworded the file.

## Estimated size

1 file, about 40 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Fix the rules first, then recompute the sample report from the corrected rules rather than
patching its numbers by hand. The sample is the worked example a reader copies, so it has to be
derivable.

- Add a Med impact rule, or delete the Med band and make impact a two-value component. Deleting
  changes the value range, so prefer adding the rule.
- State which hard override wins when both fire, and say that ties inside override 1 fall to the
  same four-key order used elsewhere.
- Recompute the sample board end to end. Check that every ROI equals value divided by the effort
  tier, that every component cited in a "why" line matches the band table, and that the counts
  sum to the stated total.
- Correct the value range in the divisor rationale to match the examples, or relabel the examples
  as atypical.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the User impact table, when a reader looks for the rule that yields Med, then the file
   states one.
2. Given a bead that is both overdue and P0, when the overrides are applied, then the file states
   which override decides.
3. Given two overdue ready beads, when the overrides are applied, then the file states how the
   tie breaks.
4. Given every row of the sample report, when each ROI is recomputed from the component tables,
   then the printed value and ROI match the computation.
5. Given the sample report's stated ready count, when the rows are counted, then they sum to it.
6. Given the divisor rationale's stated value range, when compared to every worked value in the
   file, then no example falls outside it.
notes: Found by /tadw:fresh-eyes-cr during tadw-7xq.2 on 2026-08-31, all pre-existing. Defect 3 was verified by recomputing against the Momentum band table in the same file.

title: Line-number citations into the six rewritten tracker skills are now stale
description:
## Why (Computational)

`tadw-7xq.2` rewrapped six tracker-workflow skill files at 100 columns. Every line number in
those files moved. Four documents cite them by line, and one of those citations was accurate
before the rewrap and is wrong now.

The one real regression:

- `docs/adr/0001-native-tracker-fields-are-canonical.md:12` cites
  `bead-audit/SKILL.md:92-99` for the native-field mapping table. That range held the table on
  the pre-rewrap main. It now holds the rate-limit worked example. The table moved to line 131.

Already stale before the rewrap, and listed here so one pass fixes them all:

- `docs/adr/0001-native-tracker-fields-are-canonical.md:10` cites
  `plan-to-beads/SKILL.md:486` and quotes "do not strip any section to save a line". Line 486 on
  the pre-rewrap main was a table header, and the quoted sentence exists nowhere in the file.
- `docs/plans/feature-plan-bead-refine.md:24` cites `bead-audit/SKILL.md:305` for a loop
  contract. Line 305 was the Structure points formula.
- `docs/plans/feature-plan-bead-refine.md:28` cites `bead-audit/SKILL.md:386` for a statement
  that the skill issues no tracker writes. Line 386 was "For each bead body, extract:".
- `docs/plans/feature-plan-bead-refine.md:27` cites `bead-audit/SKILL.md:10`, which was accurate
  before the rewrap and has now moved too.

ADR 0001 matters most here. CLAUDE.md calls it a rule other components obey, and names
`plan-to-beads` as citing it five times. A reader who follows its citation lands on unrelated text
and cannot check the claim.

The general defect is the citation style, not the line numbers. CLAUDE.md already states the rule
for one plan: cite by function name, never by line number. Nothing enforces it, and
`check_doc_paths.py` verifies that a path resolves without checking any line number.

## Estimated size

2 files for the citations, plus an optional checker. Band: Target.
design:
Two parts, and the second is optional.

1. Repoint the five citations above so they name a heading or quote the text, not a line number.
   `docs/adr/0001-native-tracker-fields-are-canonical.md` is the one that carries a live rule, so
   fix it first. `docs/plans/feature-plan-bead-refine.md` is a dated record, so prefer a note
   saying which heading the text sits under over a rewrite of the sentence.

2. Consider extending `skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py` to flag any
   `<path>:<line>` citation into a tracked Markdown file. A line number is unverifiable the moment
   the target is reflowed, so the check would be "do not write one", not "is this one correct".
   Weigh this against the noise it would create on legitimate citations into source code.

The epic `tadw-7xq` puts `docs/plans/*` out of scope for rewording, because a plan is a dated
record. Correcting a citation inside one is not a rewording, but keep the edit to the citation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given docs/adr/0001-native-tracker-fields-are-canonical.md, when a reader follows each of its
   citations into skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md and skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md, then each one
   lands on the text the ADR describes.
2. Given docs/plans/feature-plan-bead-refine.md, when a reader follows its three citations into
   skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md, then each lands on the text the plan describes.
3. Given the finished change, when rumdl fmt --check . and check_doc_paths.py run, then both pass.
notes: Found while shipping tadw-7xq.2. That bead's Out of scope excludes every file outside the six it rewrote, so the citations were deliberately left alone rather than fixed in passing. Bead tadw-cat also cites plan-to-beads/SKILL.md:221, but it pins the SHA 84273f4 alongside the citation, so it dates itself and needs no fix.

title: Quality-gates orchestrator gives a nondeterministic verdict on an unchanged tree
description:
## Why (Computational)

Three runs of agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md against the same fixed diff, on an
identical tree, produced three different outcomes: Gate 2 statuses WARN, WARN, FAIL, and
overall verdicts PASS, PASS, FAIL. This surfaced during the criterion-6 benchmark on
tadw-jfr (2026-08-28), run in an isolated git worktree with no other changes between runs.

A gate whose verdict flips on an unchanged tree cannot gate a push: /tadw:ship's pre-push
hook trusts the last recorded verdict (AGENTS.md, "Git hooks"), and a flip means the same
commit can read as safe or unsafe depending on which run wrote the report.

One likely confound, noted on tadw-jfr: the Project checks row (skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:90)
has no defined scope at --changed. One benchmark run executed all 12 declared commands where
the others ran 2, so the runs were not actually identical in what they executed.

## How (Algorithmic)

1. Reproduce: run the orchestrator against a fixed diff (2 files, one routing cli=coverage,
   one docs=none) three times in an isolated worktree, and diff the Gate 2 rows and the
   overall verdict across runs.
2. Pin the Project checks row's scope at --changed first (skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:90),
   since tadw-jfr identified this as the likely confound, not a property of the orchestrator
   itself.
3. Re-run the same three-way comparison after the fix. If Gate 2 and the verdict are stable
   across all three runs, the fix is confirmed. If not, keep investigating.

## Done when (Acceptance)

- Three runs of the orchestrator against the same fixed diff, on the same tree, produce the
  same Gate 2 status and the same overall verdict in every run.
- The Project checks row's scope at --changed is documented in skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md.
design: Root cause candidate: skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:90, Project checks row has no defined scope at --changed. Fix that first per tadw-jfr's notes before re-measuring.
notes: Found during tadw-jfr criterion-6 benchmarking, 2026-08-28. See tadw-jfr's 'Still open on this bead' section, item 2, for the original evidence.

title: Make the quality-gates verdict reproducible on an unchanged tree
description:
## Why (Computational)

Three runs of the quality gates against one identical tree gave Gate 2 statuses WARN, WARN, FAIL,
and overall verdicts PASS, PASS, FAIL. The measurement is recorded in tadw-jfr under "Still open on
this bead", item 2, dated 2026-08-28.

A verdict that changes on a tree that did not change cannot gate anything. `.githooks/pre-push`
reads the recorded verdict from `quality-gates-report.json` and refuses the push on FAIL
(AGENTS.md, "Git hooks"). So the flip has two costs, and they point opposite ways. A spurious FAIL
refuses a correct push, which teaches people to set `TADW_PREPUSH=off`. A spurious PASS lets a real
defect through, and nothing reports that it happened.

`/quality-gates` runs at every session close (AGENTS.md, "Landing the Plane" step 2) and
`/tadw:ship` names it as a precondition (skills/ship/SKILL.md). It is one of the most-run
components here, so the flip is not rare.

Two sources are already identified, and both are defects in `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` rather
than in the orchestrator agent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out a tree whose diff routes at least one surface to a lane, and change nothing between
   the runs. The measured case was 2 files, routing `cli=coverage` and `docs=none`.
2. Run `/quality-gates` three times against that unchanged tree.
3. Compare the three reports: the Gate 2 status, the overall verdict, the numbered case list, and
   the Project checks command list.

**Expected behavior:** all three reports agree, because nothing between the runs changed.

**Actual behavior:** Gate 2 came back WARN, WARN, FAIL, and the overall verdict came back PASS,
PASS, FAIL. One run executed all 12 declared project commands where the other two ran 2.

**Environment / version:** `main` at 50cf03a, plugin 3.3.0. Measured 2026-08-28 through
`agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md` in an isolated git worktree, recorded on tadw-jfr.

## Estimated size

2 files, about 90 LOC, band: Target.
design:
## How (Algorithmic)

Two identified sources. Fix both, then re-measure.

**Source 1: the Project checks row has no scope at `--changed`.** The Project Checks section says a
discovered command that maps to no gate "still runs", and says nothing about scope. Step 2 makes
`--changed` the default. So the two rules do not compose, and a reader can defend either reading.
In the tadw-jfr measurement one run executed all 12 declared commands where the others ran 2, which
is where most of the wall-clock scatter came from.

Pick one reading and write it into the Project Checks section. The straightforward one is that
Project checks always runs the full declared list, because those commands are project-wide and the
scope flag governs which files the gates examine, not which project checks exist. If that is too
slow, the alternative is to run only the commands whose own inputs the diff touched, which needs a
stated mapping from each command to its inputs. Do not leave both readings open.

**Source 2: Gate 2 grades on a cost judgment with no rule under it.** The grade table separates
WARN from FAIL by whether an uncovered span class "would fail expensively" against "cheap to notice
and to recover from". Step E then tells the grader to ask what a real failure would cost. That is a
fresh judgment every run, over a case list the grader also enumerates fresh in step B. Two runs can
list different cases and price them differently, and both follow the skill.

The fix is not to delete the judgment, which is what makes the gate useful. It is to make the
judgment visible and stable: require the report to carry the numbered case list and the span classes
it identified, so two runs can be compared line by line, and pin the WARN and FAIL boundary to the
categories the FAIL row already names (lost data, wrong money, a security hole, silent corruption)
rather than to the word "expensively".

**Then re-measure.** Run the same fixed diff three times with no change between runs, and compare
the reports field by field, not verdict to verdict. Two runs that agree on the verdict and disagree
on the case list are still not reproducible.

Adjacent, not the same work: tadw-qg-eval-verdict-rules-xub pins two verdict rules with single-arm
fixture evals. That asks whether one run is correct. This asks whether two runs agree.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given one fixed diff and no change between runs, when `/quality-gates` runs three times, then all three reports carry the same overall verdict and the same status for every gate.
2. Given those same three runs, when the Gate 2 rows are compared, then all three enumerate the same numbered case list and the same span classes.
3. Given those same three runs, when the Project checks rows are compared, then all three name the same command list.
4. Given the Project Checks section of `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md`, when read beside Step 2, then it states which commands run at `--changed` in one reading only.
5. Given the Gate 2 grade table, when read, then the WARN and FAIL boundary rests on the named outcome categories rather than on an unqualified cost judgment.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

The acceptance criteria below hold.

## Out of scope

- Changing what Gate 2 grades. The surfaces, the case enumeration in step B, and the span
  dimensions in step D stay as they are. This bead pins how the result is reported and where the
  WARN and FAIL boundary sits, not what the gate looks at.
- The unmeetable criterion 5 on tadw-jfr, which asks every lane start to carry
  `run_in_background: false` when this harness exposes no such parameter. That criterion needs its own rewrite, on tadw-jfr.
- Measuring the multi-lane case. All nine runs in the tadw-jfr benchmark took the single-lane path,
  and nothing has measured two or three lanes at once. Recorded there, not fixed here.

## Where the evidence lives

tadw-jfr, notes, sections "Still open on this bead" and "Caveat on the criterion 6 result, accepted
2026-08-28".

title: Carry a plan's binding ADRs into the beads plan-to-beads creates
description:

The `write-plan` skill writes a `## Decisions That Bind This Plan` section into every plan. That
section names each ADR that constrains the work and the rule it sets. `plan-review` scores its

So a constraint the author deliberately recorded stops at the plan. The bead reaches `/build`
carrying no sign of it. `/build` Phase 2 reads `docs/adr/` itself, so the constraint is not
lost outright. What is lost is the fact that the plan already decided this ADR applies here, which
is the reason a person wrote it down.

Evidence, all at `origin/main` @ 84273f45fc83debb222bab41219fe881f88d5b85:

- `skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md:221` holds the acceptance-criteria inheritance paragraph. That is
  the pattern to copy.
- `git grep "Decisions That Bind" origin/main` returns nothing.
- `skills/write-plan/SKILL.md` is absent from `origin/main`.

design:

from the plan" and modeled on it.

The paragraph tells the reader to:

1. Read the plan's `## Decisions That Bind This Plan` section.
2. For each ADR listed, decide which beads it constrains.
3. Write the ADR number and the rule it sets into those beads' `design` field. Per ADR 0001, the

title: ship: the default branch's unpushed commits are published without being reported
description:
## Why

Step 5 of the ship skill runs `git push origin main`, which publishes every
commit on the default branch, not only the landing commit the run created.
Nothing in the skill notices or reports the difference.

Observed on 2026-08-27 in the outrigger repo. `/tadw:ship` landed one squash
commit and pushed **five**: its own, plus four `outrigger-g9y` commits that had
been sitting unpushed on local `main` since the previous evening. The squash
merge itself was correct (the landing commit had one parent and carried the
whole branch diff). The four extra commits were never mentioned, in any step or
in the report, and the operator found out by reading the push output.

**The skill believes it already guards this, and the guard rests on a false
premise.** SKILL.md says:

> A failed `git pull --ff-only` means local main holds commits `origin/main`
> does not. Stop with `git-state` and change nothing.

`git pull --ff-only` does not fail when local is strictly ahead of the remote.
The merge is already up to date, so git prints "Already up to date." and exits
0. It fails only on a genuine divergence, where each side holds commits the
other lacks. In the observed run local `main` was 4 ahead and 0 behind, the pull
printed "Already up to date." with exit 0, and the run continued past the one
check that was supposed to catch this.

**The check that would have caught it is already in the file, in the wrong
place.** Step 5's rejected-push recovery contains exactly the right inspection:

```
git log --oneline origin/main..main   # must contain only the commits THIS run created
```

A run whose first push succeeds never reaches that path.

## How

1. Correct the claim in Step 4. Say plainly that `git pull --ff-only` succeeds
   when local is merely ahead, and fails only on a real divergence, so it is not
   evidence that the default branch holds nothing unpushed.
2. Run the `origin/main..main` inspection on the NORMAL path, in Step 4 right
   after the pull and before `git merge --squash`. At that moment the run has
   created no commits, so every commit the range lists is pre-existing.
3. Report them rather than stopping. These are the operator's own finished
   commits on their own default branch, and refusing to ship would strand a
   reviewed branch over work that was always going to be published by any push
   of that branch. Add a line to the "Shipped" report format that names each
   one by hash and subject and says the push carried it.
4. Keep the common case silent: a default branch already equal to its remote
   should add nothing to the report.

**Open design question, with a recommendation.** Step 3 above says report, not
stop, and that is the recommendation. The argument the other way is that
publishing commits the operator did not ask this run to publish is a side
effect, and side effects that reach a remote deserve a stop. The argument
against stopping is that it makes the skill unusable in any repository where the
default branch is routinely ahead, which is the normal state for a solo repo
that commits locally and pushes in batches. Whoever picks this up should settle
it deliberately rather than inheriting the recommendation.

## Done when

A ship from a repository whose local default branch is ahead of its remote names
every pre-existing commit its push will publish, and a ship from a repository
whose default branch already matches its remote says nothing extra.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SKILL.md no longer states or implies that a failed `git pull --ff-only` is how
  the run learns the default branch holds unpushed commits.
- Step 4 inspects `git log origin/<default>..<default>` on the normal path,
  after the pull and before the squash merge.
- The "Shipped" output format in SKILL.md gains a line for commits the push
  published that the run did not create, and the worked example shows it
  populated.
- Shipping from a default branch that is N commits ahead reports those N commits
  by hash and subject.
- Shipping from a default branch equal to its remote adds no line and no noise.
- The open design question above is resolved in the skill text, stating which
  behavior was chosen and why.
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md no longer claims a failed `git pull --ff-only` is how the run detects unpushed commits on the default branch; Step 4 inspects `git log origin/<default>..<default>` on the normal path, after the pull and before the squash merge; the "Shipped" output format gains a line naming commits the push published that the run did not create, shown populated in the worked example; a ship from a default branch N commits ahead reports those N commits by hash and subject; a ship from a default branch equal to its remote adds no extra line; and the report-versus-stop question is settled in the skill text with its reason.

## Out of scope

The evals are not part of this gate, by the repository's own rule. `tadw-routing-gaps-9wq` covers

description:

A skill that nothing loads is dead weight. Four surfaces repeat the extension-to-style-skill list,
and all four stop at Go: `skills/feature-development/SKILL.md` lines 82 to 88,

title: Author the style-markdown skill
description:
## Why (Computational)

`skills/feature-development/SKILL.md` maps file extensions to style skills, and its table at lines
82 to 88 stops at `.go`. A bead whose deliverable is a `SKILL.md` or a `docs/` page therefore falls
through to the fallback at line 96, "For an unlisted language, say so, name what you will follow
instead, and continue", and gets written with no house style at all.

In this repository that is most beads: 129 tracked Markdown files against 22 Python. The house
rules for Markdown do exist, but they ship with nothing. The em-dash ban lives in the repository
owner's private `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which no plugin consumer ever loads.

Three stakeholders, in order: the agent running `/tadw:build` here, where nearly every bead's
deliverable is Markdown; any consumer of the `tadw` plugin who writes documentation with
`/tadw:build`; and the maintainer, who currently reviews Markdown against rules that live only on
their own machine.

## Estimated size

1 file, ~300 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Write `skills/style-markdown/SKILL.md` to the sibling shape: frontmatter, a When to Use / When NOT
to Use section, a Universal Core (injected) section, numbered principles, an anti-pattern table,
and a quality checklist. `style-python` is 300 lines and `style-go` is 307; target 250 to 320.

The load-bearing constraint is the delta test. Every rule must name the layer that does not already
cover it, across three layers: rumdl's 76 rules (heading increments, fence tags, link existence and
text, table consistency), `hooks/style-core.md` (the TRUE-code principles and American spelling,
which names "documentation" explicitly), and `house-response-style` (every sentence-level rule). A
rule that cannot name such a layer does not go in. This is what keeps the skill from being a
restatement of documents the model already receives.

Key decision: one skill, not a split by audience. Both an agent-facing instruction document and a
human-facing doc are `.md`, so a two-skill split needs a rule keyed on file purpose, which the
loading skill cannot evaluate before reading the file. The agent-reader framing becomes the skill's
spine instead, stated in the opening paragraph and in the frontmatter description.

Second contribution, and it closes a live hole rather than restating anything: `hooks/preamble.js`
line 10 records that `house-response-style` is injected at SessionStart into parent sessions only,
and `subagent-start.js` calls `getStyleCorePreamble()` alone. A subagent writing Markdown, which is
exactly what `/tadw:build` produces, never receives the sentence rules. The skill instructs loading
`/response-style` alongside itself in that case.

Content kept, per the plan's delta table: who reads this document; link out instead of inlining; a
number in a document is a claim; HTML comment sentinels for machine-read regions; table versus list
versus prose at document scale; backticked path versus Markdown link; the 100-column wrap rule with
the never-reflow-a-file-you-are-only-patching rule; the em-dash and en-dash ban; the step-down rule
at document scale; the frontmatter description as an invocation contract. Cut: American spelling,
sentence-level rules, and anything mechanical that rumdl already enforces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the finished skill, when its prose is measured, then no sentence exceeds 30 words, no prose line exceeds 100 columns, and the file contains no em-dash or en-dash.
2. Given the skill, when read by someone who knows no jargon, then every rule is followable and every technical name (a path, a command, an environment variable) is kept exact.
3. Given the skill, when searched, then it contains an explicit instruction to load `/response-style` when authoring Markdown inside a subagent, and it names `hooks/style-core.md`, `house-response-style`, and rumdl as the three layers beneath it.
4. Given the frontmatter `description` read by someone who has not read the body, then it names Markdown, names the agent-reader framing, and states its trigger conditions in the third person.
5. Given `rumdl check skills/style-markdown/SKILL.md`, when run, then it exits 0.
6. Given `claude plugin validate .`, when run, then it exits 0 and reports no frontmatter error for this skill.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `skills/style-markdown/SKILL.md` exists.
- No sentence in it exceeds 30 words, measured over prose with tables and code spans excluded.
- No prose line exceeds 100 columns. Frontmatter and table rows are exempt.
- It contains no em-dash and no en-dash.
- It names `hooks/style-core.md`, `house-response-style`, and rumdl as the layers beneath it, and
  says to load `/response-style` when authoring Markdown inside a subagent.
- It states the 100-column wrap rule and the never-reflow-while-patching rule.
- `claude plugin validate .` parses its frontmatter without error.
- `rumdl fmt --check .` and `rumdl check .` both exit 0.

## Out of scope

Nothing. Registration and routing were in scope for tadw-d91 and tadw-rkx, but `hooks/test-hooks.js`
fails the moment a skill exists that `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` do not list, so they landed here.
Both of those beads are now covered by this work.
