title: Ship the bead-label hook from one source instead of copying it into every repo
description:
## Why (Computational)
label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh lives in 21 places: this source, this repo .claude/scripts copy, 10 versioned plugin-cache copies, and a working-tree copy in 9 consumer repos (atlas, compass.xyz, fathom, infra-builder, manifest, meridian, outrigger, quadrant, reach). Distribution is push-model: a human runs install_label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh from each repo root. Nothing pulls, so nothing converges on its own.

The cost is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-26 a one-line mapping bug (the reviewed label fired on every style-* skill, so an ordinary /build labeled its own unreviewed code "reviewed") had to be fixed in the source and then hand-pushed to 9 repos to take effect. Before that push, 5 of the 9 already carried the script uncommitted and drifted from their own HEAD, and an earlier same-day run had touched a different subset again. Fixing a duplication bug by duplicating resets the drift clock; it does not stop copy 22 from diverging.

The plugin cache is already a working pull-model distribution keyed by version. The per-repo copies exist to work around the hook not being consumable from there.

## How (Algorithmic)
Decide between two shapes, then do it once:
(a) Consume from the plugin. Wire settings.json at the plugin path (or a stable symlink into the active version) so `claude plugin update` is the only propagation step and the per-repo .claude/scripts copies are deleted.
(b) Keep the copy but make drift loud. Have install --check run in a pre-commit or CI job in every consumer repo, so a stale copy fails a gate rather than sitting silently for weeks.
(a) removes the class of bug; (b) only makes it visible. Prefer (a) unless a repo genuinely needs to pin or patch its own copy, in which case say so here and take (b).

Either way, reconcile the stale plugin-cache copies: 2.11.0, 2.11.1, 2.12.0 and 2.12.1 all carry the over-match, so a repo pinned to one of those keeps the bug until it upgrades.

## Done when (Acceptance)
- One place holds the hook, and a consumer repo picks up a source change without a human visiting it, OR a gate fails loudly when its copy is stale.
- No consumer repo carries an uncommitted, drifted copy.
- The chosen shape is written down, so the next person does not re-derive it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A change to the source reaches every consumer repo by one documented action, not nine.
2. install --check (or its replacement) reports in-step for every consumer, and something enforces that rather than a person remembering.
3. Whichever shape is chosen, the 9 consumer repos end with no uncommitted hook drift.

## Estimated size
Medium. Small diff in this repo, plus a settings.json change and a deletion in each of 9 consumer repos, plus one decision that should be made before any of it.

## Notes
Surfaced while fixing the reviewed-label over-match on 2026-08-26. That fix is committed here in 10f0c25 (swept into an unrelated commit by a concurrent session, another symptom worth noting) and hand-pushed to the 9 consumers.

title: Ground Gate 2's case enumeration in the project's coverage tool
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2 enumerates "each new or changed function, and each branch inside it"
(`skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:333`) and grades a case table where an empty cell is the finding
(`:391`). Nothing checks that the enumeration is complete. A branch the model overlooks in step B is
absent from the table, and the gate can still report PASS over it.

That is the one failure mode a coverage tool catches cheaply and a reader cannot. The skill runs no
coverage tool today: `--cov`, `nyc`, `simplecov`, and `lcov` appear nowhere in its 25 mentions of
"coverage".

The stakeholder is anyone who reads a PASS from the gate the skill calls its own reason to exist
(`:39`).

This does not reverse the skill's rejection of coverage percentages at `:369`, and it must not. That
argument is correct: five tests of one input class cover one point, not five, and no percentage shows
that. The tool supplies the branch inventory; the existing judgment still supplies the grade.

Grounded against origin/main @ 2cdde531e624a03d59d6934e6fe34e648a3cecf5.

## Estimated size

2 files, about 90 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add the coverage command to what Step 1 discovers, then reconcile in Gate 2 step B.

Step 1 already maps every declared command onto the gate it serves (`SKILL.md:90`). Coverage is
declared in the same places the test command is: `--cov` settings in `pyproject.toml`, `nyc`, `c8`, or
`vitest --coverage` in `package.json`, `simplecov` in the Gemfile, `go test -cover`. Discovery reads
it rather than guessing, which is principle 1 of the skill.

Gate 2 step B then does one extra thing: it compares its enumerated case list against the branches
the tool reports for the changed files only, and names every branch the tool saw that the enumeration
missed. The reconciliation is the deliverable, not the number.

Three decisions worth recording:

- **The percentage never becomes the verdict.** The gate reports the reconciliation, never a
  threshold. A project at 62% with every changed branch covered passes.
- **Changed files only.** Whole-repository coverage answers a question this gate does not ask, and it
  would fail every repository with an old untested corner.
- **No coverage tool configured is a note, not a BLOCKED.** The gate grades by enumeration alone and
  says the reconciliation did not run. Most repositories this plugin serves have no coverage tool,
  and a gate that blocks on its absence would be turned off within a week.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a repository declaring a coverage command, when Step 1 runs, then the report names that command and the file it was read from.
2. Given a change adding a function with two branches and a test covering one, when Gate 2 runs, then the report names the uncovered branch as a case with an empty cell.
3. Given a change whose enumeration omits a branch the coverage tool reports for a changed file, when Gate 2 runs, then the report names that branch as missed by the enumeration.
4. Given a repository with no coverage tool declared anywhere, when Gate 2 runs, then it grades by enumeration alone and states that the reconciliation did not run, and the verdict is not BLOCKED for that reason.
5. Given a repository at 62% overall coverage where every branch the change touches is covered, when Gate 2 runs, then the gate reads PASS.
6. Given the finished skill text, when read, then no coverage percentage appears as a pass or fail threshold, and the rule at SKILL.md:369 is still present.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Step 1 discovers a declared coverage command and names its source in the report.
- Gate 2 reports any branch in the changed files that the tool executed or missed and the enumeration
  never listed.
- A repository with no coverage tool grades exactly as it does today, with a note.
- No coverage percentage appears as a pass or fail threshold anywhere in the gate.

## Out of scope

- Whole-repository coverage, and any coverage percentage threshold.
- Installing or configuring a coverage tool in a project that has none.

title: Make the live API probe prove which server answered
description:
## Why (Computational)

Two worktrees cannot run `/quality-gates` at the same time without risking a green gate over code
that never ran.

`skills/quality-gates/scripts/probe_api.py:60` defaults `base_url` to `http://127.0.0.1:3000` when
the spec omits it. Two worktrees each running a dev server both want port 3000. The second server
fails to bind, so the second run probes the first worktree's server and reports PASS for a build it
never touched. The script already names this hazard for stale builds at `probe_api.py:32`; a wrong
worktree is the same failure from a different cause.

Everything else in the skill is already worktree-safe: the report artifact and the probe spec both
resolve their path with `git rev-parse --git-dir` (`skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:488,541`), and the
five gate scripts write to no fixed path. This is the one remaining shared resource, and it is the
port.

The stakeholder is anyone reviewing a PASS produced from a second worktree. No port scheme fixes
this alone, because the probe cannot currently tell whose server answered.

Grounded against origin/main @ 2cdde531e624a03d59d6934e6fe34e648a3cecf5.

## Estimated size

3 files, about 140 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two changes, and the first is the load-bearing one.

1. An optional `identity` object in the probe spec, such as
   `{"path": "/health", "field": "commit", "equals": "<sha>"}`. When present, `probe_api.py` requests
   it before any probe and exits with its own status when the value disagrees, so the gate reports
   BLOCKED rather than PASS. Optional on purpose: requiring a health route would block every project
   that has none, and a gate that blocks constantly gets turned off.

2. The skill populates `identity` with `git rev-parse HEAD` whenever `git worktree list` reports more
   than one worktree, and in that same case refuses to fall back to the `127.0.0.1:3000` default.
   A missing `base_url` with several worktrees present is BLOCKED with the reason, not a guess.

The decision worth recording: identity is checked, not inferred. The script never tries to work out
which server it reached from a config file or a process list. It asks the server what it is, and
compares. That keeps the check honest in the one case that matters, a server that answers correctly
for the wrong tree.

A deterministic port per worktree is deliberately out of scope. It lowers the collision rate and
stays silent when a collision happens, which is the property this bead exists to remove.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a spec whose `identity` expects commit A, when the server reports commit B, then the probe exits with the identity status and the gate row reads BLOCKED naming A and B.
2. Given a spec whose `identity` expects commit A, when the server reports commit A, then every probe runs as it does today.
3. Given a spec with no `identity` key, when the probe runs, then behavior is byte-identical to the current version.
4. Given a spec whose `identity` path returns 404, when the probe runs, then the gate reads BLOCKED with the reason, and no probe is reported as passed.
5. Given a repository where `git worktree list` reports two worktrees and a spec with no `base_url`, when the gate runs, then it reports BLOCKED and names the missing `base_url`, and sends no request to port 3000.
6. Given a repository with one worktree and a spec with no `base_url`, when the gate runs, then it probes `http://127.0.0.1:3000` as it does today.
7. Given the finished change, when `python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/test_probe_api.py` runs, then it passes and leaves no server process behind.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A probe run against a server reporting a different commit reports BLOCKED, and names both values.
- A spec with no `identity` behaves exactly as it does today.
- A repository with two or more worktrees and no `base_url` reports BLOCKED rather than probing 3000.
- `test_probe_api.py` covers all three, and still leaks no process.

## Out of scope

- Deriving a port per worktree.
- Starting or managing the project's dev server. The skill probes; it never launches.

title: Add /bead-refine, a product-value review of the backlog
description:
## Why (Computational)

Nothing in the plugin decides whether a bead deserves to exist. `skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md:8` grades a bead body for implementability, so its reader is the implementing model. `skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md:3` ranks open beads by ROI and names the next one, report-only. `commands/bead-audit-all.md` loops that audit over the whole tracker in one pass. All three assume every bead should be built.

The repository owner, acting as product owner, has no tool for the opposite question. The trigger was 27 open beads (`bd stats`) with no way to ask why any given one exists, or what a whole cluster of them is even for.

Grounded against origin/main @ 2cdde531e624a03d59d6934e6fe34e648a3cecf5: all three components above are present at those paths, and `commands/validate-plugin.md:30-31` flags only unreferenced skills and agents, so a self-contained command with no skill trips no orphan check.

## Estimated size

3 files, ~300 LOC, band: Stretch. Justification: the command carries its own full procedure because it has no skill, so one file necessarily exceeds the 77-line current longest command (`commands/bead-audit-all.md`); the other two files take one table row each.
design:
One self-contained command, `commands/bead-refine.md`, with no skill, so nothing invokes it contextually. It runs over every non-closed bead fetched by a single `bd list --status=open --json` call, which returns `description`, `design`, and `acceptance_criteria` in one shot. `bd search` is keyword-only on titles, so the command does its own semantic matching rather than delegating it.

Two modes:

- Map mode (no argument) clusters the beads semantically into 4 to 8 themes plus an explicit `Unclustered` bucket. One primary theme per bead, and it prints the count sum as a check.
- Topic mode (`/bead-refine new dialog box to capture weight`) seeds from a semantic match on the phrase, expands one hop of `bd dep list` edges in both directions, and marks every row `topic` or `adjacent`.

The yardstick: the command states the product purpose it inferred and names its source (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/products/*`, any roadmap). The author corrects it once at the top, and every later verdict cites it. The author is the decider.

Interaction: print the full theme map as a table, then offer the 3 highest-suspicion themes plus "name another" through `AskUserQuestion`. Suspicion is evidence-based: theme age, days since anything in it moved, bead count, and whether the code it targets still exists. One theme is then adjudicated per round as a numbered table, the author corrects by exception, and the writes apply in one batch.

Six verdicts, each mapping to one `bd` command:

- Keep: `bd update -p N` when the priority moves
- Shrink: rewrite the body down to the valuable part
- Merge: `bd supersede <id> --with=<keeper>`
- Defer: `bd defer <id> --reason="..."`
- Kill: `bd close --reason="refined out: ..."` plus a `refined-out` label
- Promote: `bd update -p 1`, re-parent

Every touched bead also gets a `refined:YYYY-MM` label, so a later run can offer to skip recently refined beads.

Deliberate boundaries, each with a reason:

- No numeric score. `triage-beads` owns the value-over-effort arithmetic, and two scores for one bead would contradict forever. Discipline comes from requiring a cited reason per verdict.
- Grounding is a path-existence and grep check only, reporting `target present` or `target missing`. The full Grounding Audit belongs to `bead-audit`.
- `in_progress` beads appear in the map for context and take no verdict.
- The command never files new beads. Gap-finding is `product-manager` and `/product-surface-docs`; filing is `/bead-create`. It may name a gap in one closing line.

Registration: add the command to the `AGENTS.md` registered-commands list (30 to 31), add a row to the `AGENTS.md` Task Routing table, and add a row to the `README.md` command table. Leave the pipelines in `AGENTS.md` unchanged; `docs/ROUTING.md` coverage is already tracked by tadw-routing-gaps-9wq.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a repository with a beads database and no `bv` on PATH, when `/bead-refine` runs, then it completes the theme map without erroring.
2. Given 27 open beads, when map mode renders the theme map, then it prints between 4 and 8 named themes plus `Unclustered`, and prints a count sum equal to the open bead total.
3. Given a bead that matches two themes, when the map renders, then that bead appears in exactly one theme.
4. Given `/bead-refine new dialog box to capture weight`, when the set is built, then every row is marked `topic` or `adjacent`, and no bead more than one dependency hop from a topic match appears.
5. Given a repository with no product-purpose document, when the session starts, then the command states the purpose it inferred, names the file it read, and asks the author to correct it before any verdict.
6. Given a theme of 6 beads, when the round renders, then each row carries id, title, type, priority, age, days since last touched, blocks and blocked-by counts, a one-line statement of who it serves, a grounding flag of `target present` or `target missing`, a recommended verdict, and a one-line reason.
7. Given a recommended Kill the author did not confirm, when the batch applies, then that bead's status is unchanged.
8. Given a confirmed Kill, when the batch applies, then the bead is closed with a reason beginning `refined out:` and carries the `refined-out` label.
9. Given any bead that took a verdict, when the batch applies, then it carries a `refined:YYYY-MM` label.
10. Given an `in_progress` bead in a theme, when the round renders, then it appears with no recommended verdict and takes no write.
11. Given the rendered output of any round, when read, then it contains no numeric value or ROI score.
12. Given a theme with an obvious missing capability, when the session ends, then the command names the gap in prose and files no new bead.
13. Given the finished change, when `/validate-plugin` runs, then it reports no broken cross-reference and no new orphan.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `/bead-refine` runs in any repository holding a beads database, using `bd` alone with no `bv` dependency.
- Running it with no argument produces a theme map whose counts sum to the open bead total.
- Running it with a topic phrase produces one theme whose rows say how each bead arrived.
- A theme's verdicts apply to the tracker in one batch, and nothing applies without the author's confirmation.
- The command is registered in the `AGENTS.md` command list, the `AGENTS.md` Task Routing table, and the `README.md` command table.
- The pipelines in `AGENTS.md` are unchanged.
close_reason: shipped in 2.12.0: commands/bead-refine.md, registered in AGENTS.md and README.md. Five defects found and fixed by running it against this repository.

title: publish-plugin: forbid amending a pushed release commit
description:
Cutting 2.11.0 on 2026-08-24 exposed a gap. The run pushed main at cc9647e, then found a change the changelog had missed, then amended the pushed release commit. Main can only advance from an amended pushed commit by a force-push, which the skill forbids. Recovery was a reset --soft back to cc9647e and a follow-up commit de852b9, so the release became two commits and the tag names the follow-up rather than the chore(release) commit.

Step 4 writes the changelog and Step 6 pushes, so the ordering is already right on paper. What is missing is a rule stating that the completeness pass must finish before any push, and that a pushed release commit is never amended.
design:
Three edits to skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md, plus the patch bump the fix ships under.

1. Step 4 gains a rule: the completeness pass finishes before Step 6 opens, and nothing is pushed while an entry is still owed.
2. Step 6 gains the recovery: on finding a missed entry after the push, reset --soft to the pushed commit, commit the addition on top, and tag that commit. Never amend, never force.
3. The Never list and the Quality Checklist each gain a line, so the rule is reachable from the places a run actually reads.
acceptance_criteria:
1. skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md states that the changelog completeness pass finishes before any push.
2. It states that a pushed release commit is never amended, and gives the reset --soft recovery with the tag landing on the follow-up commit.
3. The Never list and the Quality Checklist both carry the rule.
4. .claude-plugin/plugin.json reads 2.11.1 and CHANGELOG.md carries a 2.11.1 section with its compare link, and the [Unreleased] link points at v2.11.1.
5. The repository's own check list passes.
close_reason: shipped: fix: publish-plugin forbids amending a pushed release commit (tadw-e7w)

title: Add a publish-plugin skill that cuts and tags a release
description:
Publishing this plugin is entirely manual and it drifts. plugin.json sat at 2.10.1 while main ran 13 commits past the release commit, and the v2.10.0 and v2.10.1 tags were created locally and never pushed. The only automation in the path is a gate: .githooks/reference-transaction refuses a v* tag when 'claude plugin validate' fails. There is no release workflow and no publish script, and 'gh release list' returns nothing.

The marketplace pins tadw at version 'latest' against this repository's git URL, so pushing main is what actually publishes. That makes an untagged, unversioned main a published state, which is why the drift is worth closing with a skill rather than a checklist.
design:
Decide the semver bump from the changes since the last release, not from a person's mood. MAJOR for a renamed or removed component, a changed plugin name (the invocation namespace), or a broken machine-readable contract. MINOR for a new skill, agent, command, flag, or environment variable. PATCH for a fix, a doc edit, or a test-only change.

The version bump lands as its own 'chore(release): X.Y.Z' commit on main touching exactly CHANGELOG.md and .claude-plugin/plugin.json, after any feature branch has been squash-merged. Every prior release in this repository has that shape, and releases here batch several landings, so the bump cannot be tied to one branch's squash. The tag then points at a tree whose manifest states the version it claims.
acceptance_criteria:
1. skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md exists and 'claude plugin validate .' parses its frontmatter.
2. The skill derives the bump from the commits and diff since the last tag, and states the rule that decided it.
3. The skill writes the CHANGELOG version heading and the compare link footer in the existing Keep a Changelog shape.
4. The skill updates version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and commits both files as 'chore(release): X.Y.Z'.
5. The skill squash-merges a feature branch when given one, by delegating to the ship skill rather than reimplementing the land.
6. The skill tags vX.Y.Z and pushes main and the tag, and treats the reference-transaction refusal as a stop.
7. The skill is registered in the AGENTS.md name list, the AGENTS.md routing table, the README skills table, and docs/ROUTING.md, and is listed among the accepted orphans.
8. The repository's own check list passes.
close_reason: shipped: feat: Add a publish-plugin skill that cuts and tags a release (tadw-muo)

title: Stub every hook check in the pre-push fixtures
description:
## Why (Computational)

`.githooks/test_prepush.py` is 79.5s of a 148.7s ship gate, the single largest cost in the repository's own checks.

Profiled 2026-08-23: building a fixture costs 0.28s of git work, and one `git push --dry-run` costs 2.41s with the hook and 0.03s with `TADW_PREPUSH=off`. The suite makes 31 real pushes. So the cost is not the fixtures and not git; it is the hook's own checks running inside every push.

The fixture stubs 8 of the 14 checks. The remaining 6 are real, and they sum to roughly 2.3s: two style-testing scripts, two doc-path scripts, the secret scanner, and rumdl.

Re-running this repository's linters 31 times inside a suite proves nothing their own suites do not already prove, and all of those suites run in the same gate anyway.
design:
Derive the stub set from `commands_in_hook()` rather than listing it. Every hook command naming a path in this tree gets a body that exits 0, keyed by its interpreter. A check added to the hook is then stubbed automatically, which is what the current hardcoded SLOW_CHECKS map cannot do.

rumdl stays real: it is a binary rather than a file in the tree, so there is nothing to stub, and it costs 0.1s.

The suite's subject is the hook's control flow, which checks fail, which warn, which are skipped, whether a deletion is gated. Not whether the linters work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the suite, when it runs, then every check the hook invokes by path is stubbed in the fixture.
2. Given a check added to .githooks/pre-push, when the suite runs, then it is stubbed without editing the suite.
3. Given the suite, when it runs, then all 30 checks still pass.
4. Given the suite, when timed, then it completes in under 40 seconds, down from 79.5.
5. Given the repository, when the full check list runs, then every command still exits 0.

title: Bead-label hook wiring errors on every event when $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR no longer exists
description:
A session whose worktree is removed under it keeps running, and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR then names a directory that is gone. Every wired event fails at the shell level: /bin/sh reports 'No such file or directory' and exits 127, so Claude Code surfaces 'Stop hook error', 'UserPromptSubmit hook error', and 'PostToolUse:Bash hook error' on nearly every turn.

Observed 2026-08-23. A live claude process (PID 86028, started 2026-08-22) had cwd /Users/jtempleton/Dev/templeton-agentic-dev-workbench/.outrigger/worktrees/qg-prepush-verdict-gate-tug-gate-the-push-on-a-recorded-fail-verdict, which .outrigger/worktrees/ no longer contains. The scripts are tracked in git, so the copy existed while the worktree did; landing tadw-qg-prepush-verdict-gate-tug removed the worktree while the session lived on.

The hook itself is careful: every failure path inside it exits 0 so a session continues. The wiring is not, because the shell never reaches the script. So the one failure the design took most care to avoid is the one the wiring produces.
design:
Guard each wired command with a test for an executable file, and exit 0 when it is absent. Write the path twice rather than binding it to a shell variable, since a hook command string is not a place to rely on Claude Code leaving $-expansion alone.

Apply it in three places, so a repository installed later inherits the guard:
  1. .claude/settings.json here, for all four entries (three label events plus the PostToolUse close hook).
  2. HOOK_COMMAND in scripts/install_label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh.
  3. Cases in hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh.

The installer identifies its own wiring with contains($name), so the guarded string is still recognized, repaired rather than duplicated, and reported as wired by --check.

Silence is the right outcome here rather than a warning: the script that owns the log file is the missing thing, so there is nowhere to record the outage from. Restarting the session is the fix, and the guard only stops the noise.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a directory that does not exist, the wired command exits 0 and writes nothing to stdout or stderr.
2. With the script present, the wired command still runs it and still labels the bead.
3. install --check reports all three events wired against the guarded command string.
4. A second installer run still reports 'already wired' and adds no duplicate entry.
5. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
6. AGENTS.md records what a removed project directory does and what stops it.
notes: Not a fix for the zombie session that found it: a session whose project directory is gone cannot label anything, guard or no guard. End that session. The guard is about every future session that outlives its worktree.
close_reason: shipped: fix: guard hook commands against a missing project dir (tadw-1rf)

title: Bead-label hook: close the drift between source and deployed copies
description:
Deployed copies of label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh drift from the source in scripts/, and nothing reports how. The installer already reports installed / updated / already current by comparing source against destination with cmp, so drift DETECTION exists. What is missing is narrower: it never says WHAT differs, and it has no way to report drift without overwriting it.

Re-checked 2026-08-22 at main 141440f: this repository's own two copies are now byte-identical at 465 lines, so the in-repo drift the plan recorded is already closed. Fathom's copy is 18,293 bytes and carries no br references, so the br removal the plan scheduled is also already done there.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M4. Re-verify both claims before starting, since both were true of an older tree.
design:
1. Add a content hash near the top of the script, computed at install time by the installer and logged on every run. A hash rather than a VERSION string, because a hash self-maintains and a version needs a bump discipline nothing here enforces.

2. Extend the installer rather than rebuild it. Print a one-line summary of what differs before overwriting, and add a --check flag that reports drift and exits non-zero without copying, so a pre-push hook can use it later.

3. Reinstall into fathom, then confirm fathom's own suite still passes.

Do not add a tracker backend. bd only.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The installer run twice reports 'already current' the second time and copies nothing.
2. The installer against a modified destination reports what differs before overwriting.
3. --check exits non-zero against a drifted destination and copies nothing.
4. --check exits 0 against a current destination.
5. diff between the source and each deployed copy is empty, and the logged hash matches.
6. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures here, and uv run pytest -q passes in fathom.
notes:
Steps 1 and 2 landed in 14ac7f9: the runtime content hash and the installer's --check plus its drift report. Step 3 needed nothing: both copies here were already byte-identical with all three events wired.

Step 4, reinstalling into fathom, is NOT done and needs the author's call. --check reports fathom's copy carries 54 lines the source does not, and those 54 lines are an UNCOMMITTED local edit, so a reinstall would discard work that exists nowhere else. atlas is 116 lines ahead of the source in the same way, and AGENTS.md still calls atlas 'the copy of record', which conflicts with treating scripts/ here as the source. Settle which repository is the source before overwriting either.
close_reason: All four copies converged on hash 15885ca18df1 (source, this repo's deployed copy, fathom, atlas), all three events wired in each. Drift closed in both directions: fathom's prefix filter was ported up rather than overwritten.

title: Bead-label hook: make a broken hook visible
description:
The hook's header states its contract: every failure path logs to stderr and exits 0, so a skill runs whether or not the bead could be labeled. Exiting 0 is right. Logging only to stderr is what makes an outage undetectable, because hook stderr is not surfaced in normal use.

This has hidden a total outage twice. The deployed copy's own comment records the first: every label attempt between the 2026-08-12 cutover and that fix logged a failure nobody read, and no bead was labeled in that window. The second is the outrigger resolution defect (tadw-b14), found by inspection after the fact rather than by anything in the session.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M3. Cite by function name, never by line number.
design:
1. Append every invocation outcome to $GIT_COMMON/bead-label.log: timestamp, event, skill, branch, resolved id or 'unresolved', action taken. Keep stderr logging unchanged. Cap the file by truncating to its last 1000 lines when it exceeds that, checked once per invocation. The hook fires on every /simplify and /code-review in a long-lived checkout, so unbounded growth is unacceptable and a rotation scheme is more machinery than the problem needs.

2. Add a --doctor mode that resolves against the current branch and prints what it would do, writing nothing: no label, no export, no log line. It takes no hook payload on stdin and no arguments; it reads the current branch itself. Guard it before the payload read at the bottom of the script, so a missing stdin cannot hang it.

Preserve the exit-0-on-every-failure contract. This adds visibility, not a failure mode.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every invocation appends exactly one line to $GIT_COMMON/bead-label.log, carrying the branch, the resolved id or 'unresolved', and the action.
2. An unresolved run still exits 0 and still writes its line.
3. --doctor on a resolvable branch names the bead and the label, calls no bd update, and writes no log line.
4. --doctor on main reports no candidate and exits 0.
5. The log truncates to its last 1000 lines once it exceeds that.
6. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
close_reason: Implemented on branch outrigger/tadw-b14/hook-resolution-and-visibility; 173 checks pass and each fix was observed to fail against the pre-fix script

title: Take the response-style evals out of the ship gate
description:
## Why (Computational)

The `ship` skill takes its gate from the AGENTS.md "Commands for This Repo" block: 'When it declares a list, the list is the gate and every command in it must exit 0.' That block ends with `python3 evals/run.py`, so the response-style evals gate every merge.

They are the wrong shape for a gate on two counts. They are non-deterministic: `plain-sentences` grades model prose against a 35-word ceiling, and observed lengths across runs on 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23 were 40, 38, 37, 34, 26, and 22. A gate that fails at random teaches people to re-run until green, which is how a gate stops meaning anything. They also cost twelve real model calls and several minutes per run.

Measured this session: two finished, fully verified branches were blocked by that suite, once on a credential fault and once on a grader fault, neither of which the branches caused.

AGENTS.md already excludes three commands from `.githooks/pre-push` and says why for each. The ship gate has no such statement, so it takes the whole list.

The stakeholder is anyone shipping through /tadw:ship.
design:
State the ship gate in AGENTS.md the way the pre-push exclusions are already stated: in prose, beside the list, with the reason. Do not delete the command from the block. It is a real command for this repository and removing it would hide it, and `.githooks/test_prepush.py` asserts every NOT_IN_HOOK key is still present in AGENTS.md, so a deletion would correctly fail that check.

The evals stay a measurement you run deliberately, not a gate that runs on every merge.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given AGENTS.md, when the ship skill reads it for a gate, then the text names the gate as the list minus python3 evals/run.py, with the reason.
2. Given AGENTS.md, when a reader looks for the evals command, then it is still in the command block.
3. Given the repository, when python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py runs, then it passes, including its assertion that every documented exclusion is still in AGENTS.md.
4. Given the repository, when python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py runs, then every path claim still resolves.
close_reason: shipped: chore: take the response-style evals out of the ship gate (tadw-gcc)

title: Grade decision-matrix-trigger on the rule, not on bold markup
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/cases/decision-matrix-trigger` has been marked `known_failing` since 2026-08-05 and fails on every run, in both arms. Because `python3 evals/run.py` is in the AGENTS.md check list, it is the ship gate for every branch, so one red case blocks every merge in the repository.

Its note guesses the runner's output capture is at fault: 'the response DOES lead with a bold recommendation when captured by hand ... which points at the runner's output capture'. Captured through --json on 2026-08-23, the graded string begins:

    Add a nullable column.\n\n| Option | Work to build | ...

The response leads with the recommendation, on the first line, above the table. The rule is satisfied. The grader is `\\A\\s*(\\*\\*|#{2,} )`, which requires markdown bold or a heading, so it fails a response that follows the rule in plain prose.

This is the second time this case has been failed by a formatting proxy. Its own `why` records the first: an earlier pattern demanded the literal word 'recommend' and failed 3 of 3 correct responses.

The stakeholder is anyone shipping through /tadw:ship, and the author of any future style rule graded by proxy.
design:
Grade the rule the case exists to measure: the recommendation LEADS. Deterministically, that is 'the first line names one of the three options, before any table pipe'.

    \\A[^|\\n]{0,120}?(nullable column|side table|JSON)

Naming the options is specific to this case, which is correct: the case is specific, and a general 'is this a recommendation' pattern is the proxy that failed twice already.

What it accepts and rejects is the test of whether the bar moved to the right place, so pin both directions with fixtures rather than only re-running the model.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the real response captured on 2026-08-23, when the grader runs, then it passes.
2. Given a response that opens with the table and states the recommendation after it, when the grader runs, then it fails.
3. Given a response that opens with a preamble naming no option, when the grader runs, then it fails.
4. Given the case file, when it is read, then known_failing is gone and the why records what the two proxies got wrong.
5. Given the repository, when python3 evals/run.py runs, then decision-matrix-trigger passes in both arms.
close_reason: shipped: fix: grade decision-matrix-trigger on the rule, not the markup (tadw-z3q)

title: Pin the typed /quality-gates path with a UserPromptSubmit regression case
description:
## Why (Computational)

.claude/settings.json wires UserPromptSubmit to label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh so a typed
/quality-gates drops the gate marker. That command reads SKILL.md rather than invoking the
skill, so PreToolUse never fires for it and UserPromptSubmit is the only event that sees it.

hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh covers the Skill-tool path (label/pre, :586) and a typed
/tadw:build (label/prompt, :676), but no case fires UserPromptSubmit with /quality-gates. The
most-used entry point is verified by hand only. Verified working manually on 2026-08-22 against
a throwaway repo; nothing stops it from breaking silently.

## Estimated size

1 file, ~15 LOC, band: Trivial.
design:
Add one case to hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh beside the existing label/prompt case, using
the same payload helper with event UserPromptSubmit and command /quality-gates. Assert the
marker file exists and that its third line names the skill, matching what the label/pre case
asserts for the Skill-tool path.

Note for whoever writes it: the Stop path requires the report to be strictly newer than the
marker in whole seconds, so a case that writes the report in the same second reads as "the run
is still going". The existing PASS case handles this; a new one must too.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh, when it runs, then a case fires UserPromptSubmit with the command /quality-gates and asserts the gate marker is dropped naming the skill.
2. Given that case, when the UserPromptSubmit wiring is removed from .claude/settings.json or the prompt mapping is reverted in the hook, then the case fails.

title: Strip redirecting credentials before each eval model call
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/run.py` spawns `claude -p` with the parent environment inherited whole. When the shell exports `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, that key takes precedence over the stored claude.ai login and every case fails at invocation with a connectors warning that reads like a style failure. Measured 2026-08-22: 12 of 12 runs failed that way, and the harness reported 0/6 in both arms.

The same class of variable can redirect the call without failing it. `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` with `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` routes to a different account, and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` can answer with a model other than the one the run header reports.

The stakeholder is anyone who runs the declared check list from a shell that was switched to another account. `evals/run.py` is in the AGENTS.md command list, so a ship gate hits this and reports a blocked repository that is fine.

`evals/README.md` already names the fix: run `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY python3 evals/run.py` "until run.py strips that variable itself".
design:
Build the child environment in one place, at the single spawn point in `ask()`, from an explicit named tuple of the variables that redirect a call. Do not filter by prefix: `ANTHROPIC_` would also drop unrelated settings, and a named list says why each entry is there.

Strip rather than warn. A warning inside a 12-call run scrolls past, and the failure it warns about is total.

Shorten the `evals/README.md` passage to state the behavior instead of the workaround.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a shell exporting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, when a case runs, then the spawned claude process does not see that variable.
2. Given a shell exporting CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, when a case runs, then the spawned process sees neither.
3. Given any run, when a case runs, then the spawned process still sees the rest of the parent environment, PATH included.
4. Given the repository, when python3 evals/test_run.py runs, then it passes and covers the rule above without a model call.
5. Given evals/README.md, when it describes running the suite, then it no longer tells the reader to strip the variable by hand.
close_reason: shipped: fix: strip redirecting credentials before eval model calls (tadw-6x4)

title: Add the domain-modeling skill

title: Restructure the quality-gates skill's Step 4 into lanes
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 4 spans `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:196-467` as one sequential block. The orchestrator
cannot partition what the skill states as a single pass, and three cross-gate couplings currently
survive by convention rather than by statement, so a future edit breaks them silently:

- Gate 7 takes its `--base` from the SHA Step 2 resolved (`SKILL.md:102`).
- Gate 2 cites Gate 8's result, and a green Gate 8 does not satisfy Gate 2's end-to-end rule
  (`SKILL.md:217`, `:243`).
- A browser-ui surface is a HANDOFF this skill cannot settle (`SKILL.md:220`,
  `route_qa.py:85`), and it rides its own row.

## Estimated size

1 file, 180 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Partition Step 4 by the lane table in `docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md`, and state each
of the three couplings inline where the gate that depends on it is defined, rather than leaving them
to be rediscovered.

The constraint that shapes the edit: the skill must remain a valid standalone document.
`skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md:89` reads it and runs four of its gates with no agent involved,
and the plan's rollback path depends on that staying true, since reverting the feature is deleting
the agent and restoring one line of the command.

Gate semantics do not change. Only the statement of who runs each gate, and in what grouping, does.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a change with an `http-api` surface, when the report is produced, then Gate 2's end-to-end finding and Gate 8's probe result are both present and distinguishable, per `SKILL.md:243`.
2. Given a fixture diff containing a `.tsx` file, when the gates run, then a `Handoff: browser-ui` row naming `/qa` appears with a null command, Gate 2 is reported HANDOFF rather than SKIP because every routed surface was a handoff, and the verdict is INCOMPLETE.
3. Given a diff touching both an `http-api` file and a `library` file, when the gates run, then the report carries exactly one Change coverage row whose counts cover every case in the numbered case list, and the Change Coverage table carries a row for every numbered case.
4. Given the restructured skill, when `/verify-acceptance` reads it, then it runs its four gates without the agent.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

• Every gate resolves to exactly one lane or to the orchestrator
• All three couplings are stated in the skill rather than implied
• /verify-acceptance can still read the skill directly and run its four gates with no agent

## Out of scope

• Changing what any gate checks. This is a restatement of ownership, not of technique.

## Implementation (2026-08-22, commit a814d94)

Step 4 of skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md gained three subsections at its head:

- **Who Runs Each Gate**: states the standalone shape first (verify-acceptance reads this file and runs four gates with no agent), then the three-lane partition. An 11-row ownership table covers every row the report can contain, including the two rows Step 4 never defined before (handoff rows, Project checks). Also states the blocking-dispatch rule from ADR 0002 Finding 4, the undispatched-lane SKIP rule, and the missing-return BLOCKED rule.
- **What Every Lane Is Given, and What It Must Not Re-derive**: base SHA, changed paths, gate set, numbered case list.
- **Reducing Two Rows for One Gate**: per-field reduction (status, counts, evidence tables, raw output, attribution), with the handoff row exempt.

Couplings stated inline at the depending gate: base SHA at Gate 7, the Gate 8 citation at Gate 2, browser-ui HANDOFF in the new Handoff Rows subsection.

Follows ADR 0002: three lanes, not four. Gate 5 and the docs-surface Gate 2 row moved to the orchestrator.

Also added: ownership sentences in Step 5 and Step 6, two Always rules, two Never rules, two checklist items.

Gate semantics unchanged. +144/-2 lines, one file.
close_reason: shipped: chore: Restructure the quality-gates skill's Step 4 into lanes (tadw-71y)

title: Keep bead labeling working when the gates run from an agent
description:
## Why (Computational)

`.claude/settings.json:29` wires `.claude/scripts/label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh` to
`PreToolUse` with matcher `Skill`, and that copy maps `quality-gates` to inject mode at `:202-204`,
carrying the gate "the overall verdict is PASS". An agent dispatch is not a `Skill` call, so the
hook never fires and never errors: the label silently stops being applied.

The plan's risk table rates this the most likely failure of the whole change, because nothing
reports it.

Two tracked copies of the hook exist and they have diverged. The `.claude/scripts/` copy handles
`PreToolUse` and `Stop` only; the `scripts/` copy ships to other repositories, is wired to three
events, and uses gate mode instead of inject mode.

## Estimated size

4 files, 90 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Implement whichever mechanism the ADR chose: an added matcher for the agent dispatch, having the
orchestrator invoke the skill through the Skill tool so the existing matcher still fires, or
labeling from the Stop event.

Touch both copies deliberately rather than editing one and assuming they match. The `.claude/`
copy is what fires in this repository; the `scripts/` copy is what the installer distributes.

Extend `hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh` with a case that fails when the labeling path breaks. The
suite already fakes the tracker on PATH and asserts recorded argv, so the case fits the existing
harness. Without it this defect can only be found by noticing an absent label.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a /quality-gates run started by a typed command or by the Skill tool, when it starts, then the hook drops a gate-mode marker naming the bead and the skill, and injects no instruction.
2. Given <git-dir>/quality-gates-report.json written after that marker with verdict PASS, when the session stops, then the bead carries the qa-d label; given FAIL, INCOMPLETE, NO GATES RAN, or an unreadable file, then it carries no label and the marker is cleared; given a report older than the marker, then the marker is kept.
3. Given hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh, when it runs, then cases cover the marker drop and every Stop outcome above, and the PASS case fails against a copy of the hook with the JSON reader reverted.
4. Given the two copies of the hook, when the change lands, then .claude/scripts/ is byte-identical to scripts/ and .claude/settings.json wires UserPromptSubmit, so the typed /quality-gates command (which reads SKILL.md rather than invoking the skill) still drops the marker.
notes: Acceptance restated per ADR 0002, which rejected the inject instruction the original criterion 1 named. The agent path is covered by construction: Stop reads the report and never asks which tool ran.
close_reason: Labeling moved to the Stop event reading quality-gates-report.json (ADR 0002), so it survives an agent dispatch. Both hook copies byte-identical, UserPromptSubmit wired, 86 checks pass.

title: Add the quality-gates orchestrator agent with its three lane contracts
description:
## Why (Computational)

Build the agent that ADR 0002 named.
`docs/adr/0002-the-quality-gates-orchestrator-fans-out-to-blocking-subagents.md` calls it
`agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md`, and that file does not exist yet.

Without it, nothing starts the three lanes. A lane is one subagent that runs some of the gates and
returns what it found. Nothing writes the lane contract either, meaning the fixed set of fields a
lane must return.

`/quality-gates` runs at every session close (`AGENTS.md:429`, step 2 of "Landing the Plane"), and
`/tadw:ship` names it as a precondition (`skills/ship/SKILL.md:11`). Both facts make it one of the
most-run components in this repository.

## Estimated size

1 file, 220 LOC, band: Target.
design:
## How (Algorithmic)

Add one file, `agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md`. ADR 0002 Question 1 chose that name. The
command wins the shared `tadw:quality-gates` name, so `commands/quality-gates.md` reaches the agent
by its own name instead. Give the file the four frontmatter fields this repository uses (`name`,
`description`, `model`, `tools`), and follow the body shape of `agents/code-reviewer.md`.

The agent owns Steps 1, 2, 3, and 6 of the skill. No lane works out the gate set, the scope, or the
routing a second time. The agent runs `changed_set.py` once, then hands every lane the same four
things: the base SHA, the changed paths, the gate set, and the one numbered list of cases.

It starts three lanes at once: `backend-unit`, `frontend`, and `integration`
(`skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:210`). Every start carries `run_in_background: false`. ADR 0002
Finding 4 measured why. A start is asynchronous by default, so the agent can end its turn before
the lanes answer. It then loses every result and reports no error at all.

The agent runs Gates 3, 4, 5, and 6 itself (`SKILL.md:240`). Each of those is one scripted command,
and starting a subagent to run one `python3` call costs more than it saves. Gate 5 is here for that
reason alone: ADR 0002 Question 3 kept the documentation work report-only, which left that lane one
script to run and nothing else. Gate 7, the live API probe, belongs to the `integration` lane
(`SKILL.md:226`).

The agent also owns four report rows that no lane can produce. A report row is one line in the gate
table the report prints. The ownership table at `SKILL.md:219-231` names them:

- the `Handoff: mobile-ui` row
- the Project checks row (`SKILL.md:90`)
- Gate 2's own HANDOFF status, when every routed surface is a handoff (`SKILL.md:178`)
- Gate 2's SKIP row, when every routed surface is `docs` (`SKILL.md:224`)

That last row is new since ADR 0002. The documentation lane went away, and the agent took the
surface it had owned.

Merge two rows for the same gate field by field, never on the status alone. Take the worse status,
by the order the skill states. Sum the counts over every numbered case from both lanes. Splice
every evidence table in case-number order, whichever status survived. A lane that returns nothing
is BLOCKED, never PASS.

Read the ownership table from `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` Step 4, not from
`docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md`. That plan is older than ADR 0002 and still describes
four lanes (`docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md:338`). `tadw-y6h` will bring the plan up to
date. This bead does not wait for it, because the skill file already matches the ADR.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a diff with a REST surface, when the agent runs, then the report holds one row per gate the skill defines. It uses only the six statuses at SKILL.md:66-73. It adds one Handoff: <surface> row per handoff surface, and a Project checks row when Step 1 found a command that maps to no gate.
2. Given the same diff, when the agent starts the lanes, then the report's Scope line names one base SHA, and the transcript shows changed_set.py running exactly once.
3. Given a diff with no frontend files, when the agent runs, then the frontend lane's rows are reported SKIP with a stated reason, not left out.
4. Given a lane whose start is made to fail on purpose, when the agent merges the results, then that lane's gates are BLOCKED and the verdict is FAIL.
5. Given every lane start, when you read the transcript, then each start runs synchronously and blocks until the lane returns its result, before the agent's turn ends. ADR 0002 Finding 4 is the reason: an asynchronous start lets the agent's turn end before the lanes answer, losing every result with no reported error. The harness's Agent tool exposes no run_in_background parameter; agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md Step 2 achieves this by awaiting each dispatched lane before proceeding.
6. Given the same diff run three times each way, when all six runs finish, then every wall-clock time is recorded, and the agent's median is at most 10 percent slower than reading the skill directly. Accepted 2026-08-28 as directional per the caveat recorded in this bead's notes; not a precise, reproducible figure.
7. Given a run through the agent, when it finishes, then raw_output is filled in only on FAIL or BLOCKED rows whose gate ran a command. The transcript holds no test-runner output from a lane whose gates all passed.
8. Given a diff whose only surface is docs, when the agent runs, then the agent reports Gate 2 as SKIP carrying the router's reason, and starts no lane.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Running the agent against a diff with a REST surface produces one row per gate, and every row
  carries every field of the lane contract
- The report is the one the skill already specifies, with the same six statuses and the same
  verdict rules
- No lane writes the report, and no lane decides the verdict

## Out of scope

- Changing the skill's Step 4. It already matches ADR 0002, and this bead reads it as the truth.
- Pointing `commands/quality-gates.md` at the agent. That is `tadw-rex`.
- Bringing `docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md` up to date with ADR 0002. That is
  `tadw-y6h`.

## Criterion 6 measurement, 2026-08-28

Measured, then fixed, then re-measured. One fixed diff (2 files, routing cli=coverage and
docs=none), six runs per phase, arms alternated, isolated git worktree, wall clock from the
harness's own duration_ms.

| Arm | Runs (ms) | Median | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read SKILL.md directly, one context (baseline) | 252240, 263747, 273163 | 263.7 s | - |
| Orchestrator BEFORE the fix | 441530, 461984, 529056 | 462.0 s | +75.2%, FAIL |
| Orchestrator AFTER the fix | 219110, 235567, 380703 | 235.6 s | -10.7%, PASS |

Ceiling is +10%, so the allowed median was 290.1 s. Before the fix the ranges did not even
overlap: the slowest baseline run beat the fastest orchestrator run.

Cause: the diff routed to one lane. One lane overlaps with nothing, so the orchestrator paid for
a cold subagent, a second full SKILL.md read, and a dispatch-and-wait round trip to offload about
one second of test execution.

Fix: agents/quality-gates-orchestrator.md Step 2 now counts the lanes that would start. Zero or
one lane means grade the rows inline; two or more means dispatch. All three post-fix runs took
the inline path and said so in their Lanes line.

## Still open on this bead

1. Criterion 5 is unmeetable as written. It requires every lane start to carry
   run_in_background: false, and this harness's Agent tool exposes no such parameter. Step 2 now
   requires the blocking behavior and names the flag as one way to get it. The criterion's text
   still needs rewriting.
2. The orchestrator was not deterministic before the fix: three runs on an identical tree gave
   Gate 2 statuses WARN, WARN, FAIL and overall verdicts PASS, PASS, FAIL. A verdict that flips
   on an unchanged tree cannot gate a push. Not covered by any bead yet.
3. One pre-fix lane reverted and reapplied the working tree to establish attribution, which the
   skill's Never list forbids. It restored the tree and disclosed it.

## Caveat on the criterion 6 result, accepted 2026-08-28

The repository owner accepted criterion 6 as met, with this caveat recorded, rather than by
re-measuring. Read the PASS as directional, not as a precise number.

**Solid: the fan-out threshold removed the overhead.** The before and after arms do not overlap at
all, 441530 to 529056 ms against 219110 to 380703 ms. The cause is structural rather than
statistical: the agent stopped starting a helper it could not use.

**Fragile: the -10.7 percent figure itself.** The spread inside the after arm is 161593 ms, which
is 73 percent of its own median. A fourth run above about 345000 ms would move the median to
290122 ms or worse, and flip criterion 6 to FAIL. One of the three runs was already 380703 ms, so
that outcome is not unlikely.

**The scatter is a confound, not noise.** The Project checks row has no defined scope at
--changed. One run executed all 12 declared commands where the others ran 2. More runs of the same
design would add samples from a process whose inputs vary, not confidence. Pinning that scope is
the prerequisite for any future re-measurement, and it is a defect in
skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md rather than a property of this agent.

**Unmeasured: the case the agent exists for.** All nine runs took the single-lane path. Nothing
has measured two or three lanes running at the same time, which is the only case where a fan-out
can pay for itself. This repository has no browser-ui and no http-api surface, so it may rarely
produce that case at all.

Do not re-run this benchmark expecting to reproduce -10.7 percent. Fix the Project checks scope
first, or measure the multi-lane case instead.
close_reason: Agent shipped (08ed8e9, a47b81b). Criterion 5 rewritten to match the harness's actual constraint (no run_in_background param exists; Step 2 achieves blocking behavior by awaiting each lane). Criterion 6's PASS accepted directionally per the repo owner's 2026-08-28 caveat. The remaining open item, nondeterministic Gate 2 status across identical runs, is filed separately as tadw-4s5 since it is a defect in skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md's Project checks scope, not in this agent.

title: Prove a plugin agent can dispatch a subagent, then record the four decisions
description:
## Why (Computational)

The quality-gates fan-out rests on a capability no component in this plugin has ever used. None of
the twelve files in `agents/` carries a Task or Agent tool, so milestones 2 through 4 of
`docs/plans/quality-gates-agent-refactor.md` are speculative until this returns an answer.

Three further decisions block the same work:

- Whether `commands/quality-gates.md` and `agents/quality-gates.md` collide in the `tadw:`
  namespace. `AGENTS.md:262-266` rules only on command-versus-skill.
- How bead labeling survives an agent dispatch. `.claude/settings.json:29` wires the hook to
  `PreToolUse` with matcher `Skill`, which an agent dispatch is not.
- Whether the documentation lane reports drift or fixes it. `commands/quality-gates.md:39` and
  `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:695` both promise report-only, so fixing reverses a guarantee.

## Estimated size

2 files, 180 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Spike first, decide second.

The spike is one throwaway agent that dispatches a trivial subagent and returns its result, deleted
once it has answered. It is not a prototype of the orchestrator; it answers one question, can the
dispatch happen at all.

Then one ADR under `docs/decisions/`, recording all four answers. Two of them have two known
candidates each rather than open research: the namespace question resolves either by having the
command read the agent by path (the dodge it already uses for the skill) or by naming the agent
`quality-gates-orchestrator`; the labeling question resolves by an added matcher, by having the
orchestrator invoke the skill through the Skill tool so the existing matcher fires, or by labeling
from the Stop event.

title: Automate tracker sync in the repo's own pre-push hook
description: Standing instruction from the repository owner, recorded under 'The author never handles tracker plumbing' in AGENTS.md: they will never run the tracker export by hand, and they will never remember to sync the Dolt remote. Today both are manual steps a session has to remember, so bead state reaches GitHub only when someone thinks of it. The beads git hooks that used to cover part of this were switched off deliberately, because core.hooksPath now points at .githooks so the repo's own 14 CI checks run again.
design:
Put the automation in .githooks/pre-push, not back in .beads/hooks. Reasons: it is tracked in git so the author can read it, it is already the gate that runs on every push, and it keeps one hook system instead of two. The two-copy split between .githooks and .beads/hooks is exactly what caused the 12-of-14 check drift.

Shape: after the checks pass and before the push proceeds, export the tracker and stage the export if it changed. Keep it silent on success and loud on failure, per rule 3 of the AGENTS.md block.

Open design questions for the author:
  - A pre-push hook cannot add a commit to the range being pushed. Staging an export mid-push either needs an amend (rewrites the commit being pushed) or a follow-up commit (leaves the push one commit behind). Neither is obviously right. The alternative is a Claude Code Stop hook, which runs while a session is still live and can commit normally.
  - Whether to also run the Dolt remote sync, or only the text export.

BLOCKED ON A BROKEN REMOTE. The Dolt sync path is not usable as it stands:
  - bd dolt remote list prints 'origin' with the GitHub URL.
  - bd dolt show prints 'Remotes: (none)'.
  - git ls-remote origin 'refs/dolt/*' returns nothing, so no bead data has ever synced that way.
Those two commands disagree, so the remote has to be settled before any automation can rely on it. Until then, automate the text export only, and leave the Dolt sync out.

Follow the existing hook conventions: report every failure rather than stopping at the first, warn by name when a tool is missing and allow the push, and honor TADW_PREPUSH=off. Add cases to .githooks/test_prepush.py, which already drives real git push --dry-run runs in a throwaway fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A push carries current tracker state without anyone running an export command.
2. On success the hook prints nothing about the tracker.
3. On failure the hook says what failed and that beads now exist on one machine only.
4. A missing bd binary warns by name and allows the push, matching the existing convention.
5. TADW_PREPUSH=off still skips everything, including the new step.
6. .githooks/test_prepush.py covers the success path, the failure path, and the missing-bd path, and the whole suite passes.
7. The Dolt remote disagreement above is either resolved and the sync automated, or recorded as out of scope with the text export automated alone.
8. No workflow document asks a person to run an export.

title: Script the quality-gates JSON artifact write
description:
The artifact write landed as prose in `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` Step 5 (bead tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l). The model reassembles the schema on every run, and the pre-push consumer treats an unparseable or field-shifted artifact the same as no artifact: it warns and allows. So a drifted write disables the verdict gate without ever saying so, which is the exact silent-degradation failure mode the doc-freshness and secrets gates were scripted to avoid.

Design: a stdlib-only `skills/quality-gates/scripts/write_report_json.py` mirroring `check_doc_paths.py` and `check_secrets.py` conventions. It takes the gate rows and the verdict on stdin as JSON, derives head, dirty, and timestamp from git itself rather than trusting the caller to retype them, validates `verdict` against the four Verdict Rules strings, and exits 2 when the tree is not a git repository. Then point Step 5 at the script instead of at the inline python3.

Not folded into tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l on purpose: that bead's own estimate is 3 files and 80 LOC of prose, and a script plus its pinned suite is a separate unit of roughly 300 LOC.
design:
The caller resolves the artifact path with `git rev-parse --git-dir` and passes it in. The script
must not resolve it itself, and must never use `--git-common-dir` or a literal `.git/`. That table at
`skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md:637-643` is the reason: `--git-common-dir` lets every worktree
overwrite the others' verdict, and a literal `.git/` fails outright in a linked worktree because
`.git` is a file there. Scripting the write must not quietly drop the one property that makes two
worktrees safe.

title: Teach the eval harness to run in a fixture repository
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/run.py` hardcodes `cwd=REPO_ROOT` inside `ask()`, so every case runs against
this repository and no case can plant a defect. That single line is why the skill's behavior has
never been tested.

The stakeholder is any future editor of `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md`, who today has no
regression signal at all: every rule not converted into a script is unprotected prose.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 160 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two optional `case.json` keys, both backward compatible with the six existing
cases.

A `fixture` key names a directory under `evals/fixtures/`. The harness copies it to a temp
directory, initializes it as a git repository with one commit, applies the case's planted defect,
and passes that directory as `cwd` instead of `REPO_ROOT`.

A `single_arm` key runs only the with-plugin arm. A slash command does not exist without the
plugin, so a baseline arm would measure nothing and would double the cost of every run. This is
recorded as D7 in the plan.

Keep the existing regex graders. These assertions are about which verdict and status words appear
in the report, which `require_regex` and `forbid_regex` already handle well. No judge is needed,
and adding one would make the suite nondeterministic for no gain.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the six existing cases, when `python3 evals/run.py` runs, then all six behave exactly as before the change.
2. Given a case with a `fixture` key, when it runs, then the model's working directory is a temp copy of that fixture with its own git history, not the repository root.
3. Given a case with `single_arm` set to true, when it runs, then only the with-plugin arm executes.
4. Given `evals/README.md`, when reading it, then both keys are documented with the reason fixture cases skip the baseline arm.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `run.py` honors `fixture` and `single_arm`, both optional
- The six existing response-style cases pass unchanged
- A fixture case runs against a temp git repository, not the repository root
- `evals/README.md` documents both keys and why fixture cases are single-arm

## Out of scope

The fixture cases themselves. Those are the two eval-case beads that depend on this one.

title: Pin the verdict rules and the finding cases with four fixture evals
description:
## Why (Computational)

Commit `a093acc` fixed a bug where every gate skipped and the skill still reported
PASS, and a second where a configured-but-unrunnable tool degraded to SKIP instead of BLOCKED.
Both fixes live in prose, and nothing tests them, so the next edit to the Verdict Rules can
reintroduce either silently.

The stakeholder is the owner, who would then ship the regression in a release. These two rules
are the ones the skill's own text calls the reading it exists to refuse.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

8 files, about 230 LOC, band: Stretch. Justification: four fixture repositories on one shared harness, merged from two beads that each estimated 5 files; building the harness twice cost more than one Stretch bead does.
design:
Four fixture repositories and four single-arm cases, on one shared harness.

Verdict rules:

- `gates-blocked-not-skip` configures a type checker in `pyproject.toml` that is absent from PATH.
  It asserts the report grades that gate BLOCKED with an overall FAIL, and forbids SKIP for it.
- `gates-all-skip` is a repository where every gate legitimately skips. It asserts NO GATES RAN and
  forbids PASS.

Finding cases (merged in from tadw-qg-eval-finding-cases-29f):

- `gates-untested-change` plants a new function with a branch and no test anywhere. It asserts the
  change-coverage gate reports FAIL with the case enumerated, not merely that something failed.
- `gates-planted-secret` plants a fake `AKIA` key in a source file. It asserts the secrets gate
  reports FAIL with a `file:line`, and that the key itself never reaches the report.

The decisive step is proving each test fails when its rule is reverted by hand. A model can produce
the right verdict word by luck, so a test never observed failing is not yet a test. Revert the
missing-binary-to-BLOCKED mapping in `SKILL.md`, confirm the case fails, then restore the line, and
do the equivalent for each of the other three.

Merged by /bead-refine on 2026-08-24, superseding tadw-qg-eval-finding-cases-29f. The two beads
described the same work twice: same design sentence, same plan milestone M6, same size estimate. The
fixture harness is the actual cost here, and building it twice was the waste. Two gates are graded on
verdict rules and two on findings, but all four ride one harness.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the `gates-blocked-not-skip` fixture, when the case runs, then the report contains BLOCKED and an overall FAIL, and does not grade that gate SKIP.
2. Given the `gates-all-skip` fixture, when the case runs, then the report contains NO GATES RAN and does not report PASS.
3. Given the `gates-untested-change` fixture, when the case runs, then the change-coverage gate reports FAIL and the report enumerates the untested case.
4. Given the `gates-planted-secret` fixture, when the case runs, then the secrets gate reports FAIL with a `file:line`, and the planted key string appears nowhere in the report.
5. Given each of the four rules reverted by hand in turn, when its case runs, then that case fails; when the rule is restored, it passes.
6. Given three runs of each case, when the suite finishes, then all four pass three times each.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- All four fixtures exist, each with its own repository under the eval harness
- Each case passes three runs out of three with the plugin loaded
- Each case has been observed failing once, with its rule reverted by hand, and the rule restored
- The planted key never appears in any report the suite produces

## Out of scope

- Wiring these cases into a git hook. `AGENTS.md` states that no hook runs anything under `evals/`,
  and that decision is not reversed here.

title: Require evidence citations in the change-coverage gate
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2 tells the model to read every test it counts and leaves no artifact proving
it did, so a plausible coverage table and a fabricated one look identical to the reader.

The stakeholder is whoever acts on a PASS from the gate the skill calls its own reason to exist.
Gate 2 is the difference between this skill and running the test command by hand, and today it
is the least verifiable thing in the report.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M3)

## Estimated size

1 file, about 45 LOC changed, band: Target.

Require each counted unit test to cite the `file:line` of its key assertion, and
each end-to-end claim to quote the single line driving the real entry point (the
`subprocess.run`, the HTTP client call, the CLI runner invocation).

Quoting that line is the load-bearing part. It is what separates a real end-to-end test from an
in-process call of the handler, which the gate already forbids in its Never list but currently
has no way to detect.

Mirror the requirement in three places so it survives a partial read: Gate 2 step C, the Critical
Rules "Always" list, and the Quality Checklist. Update the Output Format worked example so the
shape is visible, not just described.

1. Given `SKILL.md` after the change, when grepping for "Cite", then three hits appear: step C, the Always rule, and the checklist item.
2. Given the Output Format example, when reading the Change Coverage table, then at least one unit cell carries a `file:line` and one end-to-end cell carries a quoted line.

- The Output Format example shows a `file:line` unit cell and a quoted entry-point end-to-end cell

title: Write the verdict as a JSON artifact
description:
## Why (Computational)

The report is markdown only, so no tool can read the verdict and nothing downstream
can act on it. The immediate stakeholder is the pre-push hook, which cannot gate on a conclusion
it cannot parse.

This bead also repairs a contradiction it would otherwise create. The skill states twice that it
edits nothing (`SKILL.md:356` and the checklist item at `SKILL.md:387`), and writing an artifact
makes both statements false. A skill that violates its own Critical Rules on every run is worse
than no artifact.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M4)

## Estimated size

3 files, about 80 LOC changed, band: Target.
design:
After emitting the markdown report, write `.git/quality-gates-report.json`
carrying `version`, `head`, `dirty`, `timestamp`, `scope`, `gate_source`, `verdict`, and a
per-gate array of name, status, command, and detail. Skip the write with a noted reason when the
tree is not a git repository.

Inside `.git/` on purpose: per-clone, never committed, no `.gitignore` entry needed, and it
survives until the push it is meant to inform.

The `dirty` field is recorded for a human reader and deliberately has no automated consumer. The
skill runs before the commit almost every time, so nearly every honest report is dirty, and a
hook gating on it would block constantly.

`verdict` carries one of the four Verdict Rules outcomes verbatim: PASS, FAIL, INCOMPLETE, or
NO GATES RAN.

Then narrow the two report-only rules from "writes nothing" to "writes nothing in the working
tree", and move every copy of that claim together. `commands/quality-gates.md` line 22 states it
a third time, and `skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md` may restate it. A surviving absolute
version is worse than none, because the next reader trusts the weaker one.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a run of the skill in a git repository, when it finishes, then `.git/quality-gates-report.json` exists and its `verdict` is one of PASS, FAIL, INCOMPLETE, NO GATES RAN.
2. Given the same run, when reading the JSON, then every gate in the markdown table appears in the `gates` array with the same status.
3. Given a run outside a git repository, when it finishes, then no artifact is written and the report states why.
4. Given the three files that state the report-only rule, when grepping for "edit" and "No file", then every hit carries the working-tree qualifier.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Step 5 writes the artifact, and skips it with a noted reason outside a git repository
- The schema carries version, head, dirty, timestamp, scope, gate_source, verdict, and gates
- `verdict` is one of the four Verdict Rules outcomes verbatim
- `SKILL.md:356` and `SKILL.md:387` carry the working-tree qualifier
- No absolute "edits nothing" claim survives in `commands/quality-gates.md` or `verify-acceptance`

## Out of scope

Reading the artifact. The pre-push consumer is the "Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict"
bead, which depends on this one.

title: Script the changed-set resolution
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 2's changed-set is two git commands plus a base-resolution fallback that the
model retypes on every run, and getting it wrong silently narrows every gate.

The prose warns about one specific trap: `git diff "$BASE"...HEAD` stops at the last commit, and
this skill runs before a commit more often than after one, so the very work being checked drops
out of scope.

The stakeholder is anyone reading a scoped report that quietly covered nothing.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 230 LOC, band: Target.
design:
A stdlib Python script resolving the base by merge-base against `origin/HEAD`,
falling back to `origin/main`, then printing the union of `git diff --name-only "$BASE"` and
`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, one path per line.

The key decision is a distinct exit 3 for an unresolvable base, so the skill can tell "no remote,
fall back to --all" apart from "empty diff". The current prose conflates those two, and treating
one as the other narrows every gate to nothing while reporting confidently.

The resolved base SHA goes to stderr so stdout stays a clean path list a caller can pipe without
filtering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a repository with a committed change, a staged change, an unstaged change, and an untracked file, when the script runs, then all four paths appear on stdout.
2. Given a repository with no remote, when the script runs, then it exits 3.
3. Given any successful run, when stdout is captured alone, then it contains no SHA and every line is a path.
4. Given a file listed in `.gitignore`, when the script runs, then that file does not appear in the output.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `changed_set.py` runs with bare `python3` and prints one path per line on stdout
- The resolved base SHA appears on stderr, never on stdout
- An unresolvable base exits 3, distinct from both success and error
- The suite covers committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes all appearing, plus a
  repository with no remote

## Out of scope

Wiring the script into `SKILL.md` Step 2. That belongs to the "Point the skill at the three gate
scripts" bead.
