title: Script the hygiene marker count
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 7 is a one-line shell recipe carrying a subtle trap: `grep -c` exits 1 when it
counts zero, which is the clean result, so the `|| true` is load-bearing and easy to drop when a
model retypes it.

The stakeholder is the reader of a report where a clean hygiene gate was recorded as BLOCKED,
which reads as a broken toolchain rather than as good news.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 200 LOC, band: Target.
design:
A stdlib Python script taking `--base`, counting `TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK`, and
`XXX` on added diff lines only.

The one real decision is excluding the `+++` header line. It starts with `+` and carries a path
that can itself contain a marker word, so a naive `^+` match counts a file named `TODO.md` as a
marker. That is the false positive the current shell recipe would produce.

Exit 0 at zero (the skill maps this to PASS), 1 above zero (WARN), 2 operator error (BLOCKED).
The zero-count case must exit 0 rather than any non-zero code, which is the whole reason the
current recipe needs its `|| true`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a diff adding two lines containing TODO and FIXME, when the script runs, then it exits 1 and reports 2.
2. Given a diff whose only marker sits in a `+++ b/TODO.md` header line, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and reports 0.
3. Given a diff that deletes a TODO line and adds none, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and reports 0.
4. Given a clean diff, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and reports 0.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `check_hygiene.py` runs with bare `python3` and accepts `--base`
- The suite covers a diff adding two markers, a diff removing one, a `+++ b/TODO.md` header, and
  a clean diff
- A zero count exits 0, never a code the skill would read as BLOCKED

## Out of scope

Wiring the script into `SKILL.md` Gate 7. That belongs to the "Point the skill at the three gate
scripts" bead.
close_reason: done

title: Script the secrets gate
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 6 lives as prose regexes and exclusion lists in `SKILL.md`, so the model
reassembles the pattern set, the exclusions, and the untracked-file scan on every run, and two
runs can disagree. The doc-freshness gate already proved this fails: its prose version reported
194 false positives on first contact with a real repository.

The stakeholder is anyone trusting a PASS from the secrets gate, since a quietly narrowed
pattern list reports clean while a key sits in the tree.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 330 LOC, band: Stretch.

Stretch is justified because the script and its pinned suite are one unit. Shipping the script
without the suite would land unverified detection logic, which is the exact failure this bead
exists to prevent.
design:
Port the Gate 6 rules verbatim into a stdlib-only Python script mirroring
`check_doc_paths.py` conventions: argparse, exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 operator error, and a
module docstring stating why the script exists.

Two checks. Secret-file names across both `git ls-files` and `git ls-files --others
--exclude-standard`, covering `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.p12`, `id_rsa`, `*.keystore`,
`*credential*`, and excluding `.env.example`, `.env.sample`, `.env.template`. Then prefixed key
formats in content only: `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, `ghp_`, `xox[baprs]-`, `sk-ant-`, and
`-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----`. Generic long hex or base64 matching is deliberately absent;
it fires on lockfile hashes and minified assets, and a gate that cries wolf gets ignored.

The load-bearing design constraint is that the matched value never reaches output, only
`file:line` and the pattern name, so the report cannot copy the secret into one more place.

A comment block at the top of the test file maps each prose rule to the test pinning it. That
mapping is what proves the port neither narrowed nor widened detection.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a temp repository with an untracked, unignored `.env`, when the script runs, then it exits 1 and names that file.
2. Given the same fake `AKIA` key in `src/` and in `node_modules/`, when the script runs, then only the `src/` hit is reported.
3. Given any finding, when the report prints, then it contains `file:line` and the pattern name, and does not contain the matched value.
4. Given this repository as the working tree, when the script runs, then it exits 0.
5. Given the test suite, when it runs with bare `python3`, then every test passes and no third-party module is imported.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `check_secrets.py` runs with bare `python3` and imports nothing outside the standard library
- Running it against this repository exits 0
- The suite covers a tracked `.env`, an untracked-but-unignored `.env`, an excluded
  `.env.example`, a fake `AKIA` key in source, the same key under `node_modules/`, and a clean tree
- A test asserts the planted key's value reaches neither stdout nor stderr
- A comment block maps every Gate 6 pattern and exclusion to its test

## Out of scope

Wiring the script into `SKILL.md`. That is the "Point the skill at the three gate scripts" bead,
which depends on this one.
close_reason: Graded ACCEPTED by /verify-acceptance twice: on first pass, and again as a regression re-grade after f8259ea changed the artifact. All 5 criteria and all 5 Done-when items PASS, 44 of 44 tests in test_check_secrets.py, and the script exits 0 against this repository.

title: Remove the 104 remaining em-dashes across 10 agent, command, and skill files
description:
The house style rule forbids em-dashes and en-dashes everywhere: prose, code, comments, commit messages, docs, and UI copy. 104 occurrences remain across 10 files in `agents/`, `commands/`, and `skills/`. Release 2.4.1 cleaned only the nine in `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

One subset is worse than the rest. Some of these sit inside **output templates that an agent fills in and emits**, not in prose describing the agent. `agents/product-analyst.md:78` is `- **Feature Name** <em-dash> Description`, inside that agent's Output Format block alongside `[2-3 paragraphs providing...]` placeholders. Every product analysis that agent writes therefore carries em-dashes into a delivered document. That is the rule being broken at runtime, in work handed to a reader, rather than in a file only a maintainer opens.

Counts by file: `agents/product-analyst.md` 31, `skills/agentic-clean-code/SKILL.md` 19, `agents/diagnostician.md` 14, `skills/business-ideas/SKILL.md` 14, `skills/architecture-decision-record/SKILL.md` 11, `skills/idea-wizard/SKILL.md` 9, `commands/diagnose.md` 2, `commands/product-analysis.md` 2, `commands/quality-gates.md` 1, `skills/production-ops/SKILL.md` 1.
design:
Do the template files first, in their own commit, because they leak into generated output: `agents/product-analyst.md`, `agents/diagnostician.md`, and `skills/architecture-decision-record/SKILL.md`. The prose remainder can follow in a second commit.

Do **not** run a blanket `sed`. The replacement is context-dependent and a global substitution produces wrong punctuation:

- Term followed by a definition in a list: use ` - `, matching the convention the registered-component lists in `AGENTS.md` already use.
- A parenthetical clause inside a sentence: use a comma pair, or parentheses.
- A heading label such as `### Pipeline A <em-dash> Business Planning`: use a colon.

Read each line and choose. 104 lines is small enough that judgment beats automation here.

Prevent regression with a check. `hooks/test-hooks.js` is the existing home for repo-wide assertions and runs on Node built-ins only, so add the scan there rather than introducing new tooling. The check must exempt nothing silently: if a file genuinely needs a dash character, it should fail and force an explicit decision.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A scan for U+2014 (em dash) and U+2013 (en dash) over `agents/`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `README.md`, and `AGENTS.md` returns zero matches. Use the scan added in criterion 4 as the authority, so the bead and the check agree on one definition of "clean".
2. Replacements are context-appropriate, not mechanical: spot-checking ten changed lines shows list definitions using " - ", parentheticals using commas or parentheses, and heading labels using a colon.
3. The template subset (`agents/product-analyst.md`, `agents/diagnostician.md`, `skills/architecture-decision-record/SKILL.md`) lands in its own commit, ahead of the prose remainder.
4. A check in `hooks/test-hooks.js` fails when any tracked markdown file outside the documented exemptions contains U+2014 or U+2013. Verified to discriminate by adding one and observing a non-zero exit.
5. The exemption list, if any, is written in the check itself with a reason per entry, not implied by a path glob.
6. `node hooks/test-hooks.js` passes and its stated check count matches the number it runs.
7. No prose was reworded beyond the punctuation change. Verified by reading the diff: every hunk changes punctuation only.
notes:
Done when no em-dash or en-dash remains in any file this repo owns, and a new one cannot be added without a test failing.

Deliberately out of scope: `CHANGELOG.md` history below the current release, since rewriting shipped release notes changes the record of what was said at the time.

## Estimated size

11 files (the 10 carrying dashes, plus `hooks/test-hooks.js` for the regression check), ~134 LOC, band: Too big by file count (provisional - inferred from the How, author to confirm).

The LOC is well inside Target; only the file count pushes it over. The How already sequences this as two commits, template subset first and prose remainder second, so splitting the bead along that same seam gives two Target-band beads: the template subset is 3 files plus the check, and the remainder is 7 files. Split before claiming.

title: Cover the drifted and satisfied grounding band ceilings with a pinned fixture repository
description:
The Grounding Audit added in 2.4.1 applies two band ceilings: `drifted` caps a bead at Adequate, `satisfied` caps it at Weak. Neither ceiling has ever fired in a test.

The eight existing fixtures under `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/` are pasted bodies that name no repository of record, so all eight are `ungroundable`, which applies no ceiling. They prove the ceilings do **not** fire when they should not, and prove nothing about whether they fire when they should. The only check on that arithmetic today is a worked-example table in `SKILL.md`, which is prose an author wrote, not a computation anyone ran.

This matters more than a typical coverage gap because a ceiling that silently stops working produces a *higher* score, not a lower one. A regression here reports a stale bead as Excellent, which is exactly the failure the Grounding Audit was built to prevent.
design:
The obstacle is that grounding needs a real repository at a known sha, and the current suite is pasted text with no repo behind it.

**Option A: a committed fixture repository.** Add `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/repo/` as a small tree of real files, plus fixture beads that name it as their repository of record. Self-contained and offline, but a nested git repository inside this one is awkward to commit and easy to break.

**Option B (preferred): ground against this repository at a pinned sha.** Write fixture beads whose claims reference real paths in `tadw` at a specific commit, chosen so the outcome is fixed forever. A `drifted` fixture claims a file that was renamed between two known commits; a `satisfied` fixture states an end condition that a known commit already satisfies. Store the sha in the fixture body, and have the check pass it explicitly rather than resolving `origin/main`, so history moving does not change the answer.

Option B needs no nested repository and exercises the real `git show` and `git grep` path. Its risk is that a fixture reads as a repo-history trivia question, so each one must state in a comment which commit it pins and why that commit makes the outcome permanent.

Add at minimum: one `drifted` fixture whose expected band would be Excellent but is capped to Adequate, and one `satisfied` fixture capped to Weak. Extend `references/fixtures/README.md`, which currently documents these two states as deliberately uncovered.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A fixture exists whose grounding verdict is `drifted`, whose raw score would band Excellent, and whose expected band is Adequate.
2. A fixture exists whose grounding verdict is `satisfied` and whose expected band is Weak.
3. Both fixtures pin an explicit sha in their body, and re-running them after new commits land on main produces the same verdict. Verified by running them twice with a commit in between.
4. Each fixture states, in the fixture itself, which commit it pins and why that commit fixes the outcome permanently.
5. Discrimination is verified, not assumed: deleting the `drifted` ceiling row from the rubric makes fixture 1 report Excellent and fail; deleting the `satisfied` row makes fixture 2 fail.
6. The eight existing fixtures still report their documented bands, confirming the new fixtures did not change how the ungroundable path behaves.
7. `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/README.md` no longer says the two ceilings are uncovered, and the matching sentence in `AGENTS.md` and the Known issues entry in `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.
notes:
Done when removing either ceiling from the rubric makes a fixture fail.

Not done when a fixture merely exists and reports the right band. The test is discrimination: an untested guard and a guard that cannot fail are the same thing.

## Estimated size

~4 files (2 new fixture bodies, `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/README.md`, and the matching sentences in `AGENTS.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`), ~150 LOC, band: Target (provisional - inferred from the How, author to confirm).

title: Diagnose why the sentence limit fails in self-reports
description:
## Why (Computational)

The twenty-five-word sentence limit is the least enforced rule in house-response-style, and it
fails in the one place an agent writes most often: reporting its own work.

Measured 2026-08-05 on evals/cases/self-report-plainly at five runs, sonnet, with-plugin arm:
four of five runs broke the grader's 35-word ceiling, at 44, 48, 54, and 64 words. The skill's
own limit is 25. The label check passed 5 of 5 in the same runs, so this is not a wording
problem in the label rule.

This was invisible until PR #20. The flat label ban failed every run first, so the runner never
reported the sentence failures underneath it. Removing one failure exposed another.

The stakeholder is the reader of every agent report, who gets a 64-word sentence carrying four
joined claims where the rule promises two short ones.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out main with the plugin loaded.
2. Run `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY python3 evals/run.py --case self-report-plainly --runs 5 --model sonnet`.
3. Read the `max_sentence_words` result for each of the five runs in the with-plugin arm.

**Expected behavior:** every sentence in the self-report sits at or under the 25-word limit the
skill states, and therefore comfortably under the grader's looser 35-word ceiling recorded at
`evals/cases/self-report-plainly/case.json:5`.

**Actual behavior:** four of five runs exceed 35 words, at 44, 48, 54, and 64. The label check
passes 5 of 5 in the same runs, so the failure is specific to sentence length.

**Environment / version:** sonnet, with-plugin arm, measured 2026-08-05 on main as of PR #20.
design:
Three hypotheses, to be tested one at a time, each with a five-run measurement:

H1. The prompt invites it. The case asks for 'one short paragraph of plain prose', and a model
reads 'paragraph' as one narrative unit, then joins clauses to fill it. Test by adding a second
prompt that asks for a report with no shape constraint, and comparing sentence lengths.

H2. The rule is too far from its use. The split-word list ('which', 'so', 'but', 'since',
'because') lives in STE rule 6. The 'Report your own work plainly' section does not reference
it, so the model applies the contract without applying the limit. Test by adding one sentence
to that section pointing at the cut list.

H3. The limit is unreachable for this content. A self-report carries four facts (count,
failure, action, reason), and four facts may not fit two sentences under 25 words each. Test by
writing the target answer by hand and counting.

Change one thing per measurement. Do not lower the 35-word grader ceiling: it is already looser
than the 25-word rule, and loosening it again would stop it measuring anything.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the three hypotheses, when each is tested at five runs, then the result of each is written into the bead or into evals/README.md, naming which one held.
2. Given the chosen fix, when evals/cases/self-report-plainly runs at five runs, then max_sentence_words passes at least 4 of 5.
3. Given the same five runs, then the label check and all four substance checks still pass 5 of 5, so the fix did not trade one rule for another.
4. Given the fix, when evals/run.py is inspected, then the max_sentence_words ceiling is still 35 and the skill's stated limit is still 25.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- The diagnosis names which hypothesis held, with the run counts behind it.
- self-report-plainly passes max_sentence_words at least 4 of 5 without any grader loosening.
- The label and substance checks are unchanged at 5 of 5.

## Scope boundary
Changing the 25-word rule itself is OUT of scope. If the measurement shows 25 is unreachable
for a four-fact report, that is a finding and a follow-up bead, not an edit made under this one.

## Estimated size
1 to 3 files (the `house-response-style` section, possibly one new eval case), ~40 LOC, plus
15 to 25 model runs. Band: Target (provisional - the LOC is inferred from the How, author to
confirm; the run count is effort, not diff, and does not enter the band).

title: Fix false plugin.json component-registration claims in AGENTS.md
description:
## Why (Computational)

AGENTS.md makes three false claims about .claude-plugin/plugin.json:

- Line 355: plugin.json "defines plugin metadata, component registration, and the hooks field"
- Line 529 (Adding a New Skill): "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed"
- Line 537 (Adding a New Agent): "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed"

plugin.json is 511 bytes containing name, version, description, author, license, and hooks. It
registers zero components. `grep -c "style-python\|style-frontend\|review-python"
.claude-plugin/plugin.json` returns 0. Skills, agents, and commands are auto-discovered from their
directories; the real registration surfaces are the AGENTS.md component lists and the README table.

This is not cosmetic. The defect already produced an unsatisfiable acceptance criterion in this
tracker: bead tadw-wdk's original AC #3 required `grep -rw style-testing
.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to match, which can never pass. Every agent or human who follows
AGENTS.md to add a component will keep generating the same bad work item until the instruction is
corrected. The stakeholder is anyone extending this plugin, including future agent sessions.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing-part-2.md (M4)

## Estimated size
1 file, about 6 lines changed. Band: below Target. Justified as a standalone bead because it is
independent of all style-testing work and blocks nothing.
design:
Fix the instruction, not just the description (D11). Correcting line 355 alone would leave 529 and
537 still telling readers to edit plugin.json, and those two lines are what actually caused the
defect.

- Line 355: state that skills, agents, and commands are auto-discovered from their directories,
  and that plugin.json carries metadata plus the hooks field only.
- Lines 529 and 537: replace "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed" with the true
  surfaces, namely the AGENTS.md component lists and the README.md table.

Sequence after Part 1 (tadw-wdk). Part 1's M3 also edits AGENTS.md, at lines 168 and 362. The
concerns are disjoint (component lists versus plugin.json claims) but running both concurrently
against the same file invites a needless conflict.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given `grep -n "plugin.json" AGENTS.md`, when run, then no matching line instructs registering a skill, agent, or command in plugin.json.
2. Given a reader follows the AGENTS.md "Adding a New Skill" steps end to end, when they finish, then they have edited no file under .claude-plugin/.
3. Given AGENTS.md line 355, when read, then it states that components are auto-discovered from their directories and no longer claims plugin.json performs component registration.
4. Given AGENTS.md lines 529 and 537, when read, then each names the AGENTS.md component list and the README table as the registration surfaces.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- No line in AGENTS.md instructs registering a component in .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
- Line 355 describes auto-discovery and scopes plugin.json to metadata plus the hooks field.
- The "Adding a New Skill" and "Adding a New Agent" steps name the true registration surfaces.

## Note
plugin.json itself is NOT changed. The auto-discovery behavior is correct; the documentation
describing it is what is wrong.
close_reason: Fixed in 1.18.1: AGENTS.md no longer claims plugin.json performs component registration, and the Adding a New Skill/Agent steps name the real surfaces

title: Keep the source that raised a question when the agenda item is answered
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 6 of skills/research-synthesize/SKILL.md replaces the whole agenda line when a question is
answered. The original line names the source that raised the question, and the answered line
drops it. The provenance disappears at the exact moment the question becomes citable, so a
reader of Research/questions.md can no longer tell which source put the question there.

Found by running the skill against a fixture vault on 2026-09-01, while verifying tadw-x8b.5.

## Estimated size

1 file, 15 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Change the answered-line format in Step 6 so it carries both the link to the question page and
the source that raised the question.

The unanswered line already names the source, so the answered line should keep that clause
rather than replace it. One shape that works:

- [x] [[Does X Cause Y]], answered 2026-09-01, confidence: moderate, raised by [[Source Page]]

Update the Quality Checklist row that checks the agenda line, so the new clause is checked too.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a question raised by a named source, when the skill marks its agenda item answered,
   then the line still names that source.
2. Given Step 6 is read, when its example line is compared with the unanswered line above it,
   then no information present in the unanswered line is missing from the answered one.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Step 6's answered-line example carries the source that raised the question.
- The Quality Checklist row for the agenda line names that clause.

Backfilling the clause into agenda lines already written. No vault has one yet.

title: Feed the research agenda from each ingest
description:
## Why (Computational)

Every ingest writes an Open Questions section that nothing ever reads, so the questions a source
raises die on the page that raised them. The agenda is what lets a later ingest or a synthesis

Source: docs/plans/feature-plan-research-brain-upgrade.md, milestone 5.

Extend Step 7 of skills/research-ingest/SKILL.md so the log update also appends each of the

Step 7 is the right home because it already owns the bookkeeping writes, so the agenda cannot
drift out of step with the log.

1. Given an ingest whose source page lists Open Questions, when the ingest completes, then each
   question appears in Research/questions.md.
2. Given an appended agenda item, when it is read, then it names the source that raised the

- Each appended item names the source that raised the question.

title: Report which skills loaded, and add the verify-app invocation case
description:
## Why (Computational)

This repository has twice shipped a skill that was well written, registered, and never loaded,
recorded in `docs/eval-driven-development.html` section 1. The `verify-app` skill is worth nothing if
it does not fire when a person asks whether a change works. The harness cannot measure that today:
`ask` in `evals/run.py` returns plain text and cannot see which skills loaded.

## Estimated size

4 files, 170 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Change ask in evals/run.py to run claude -p with --output-format stream-json, parse the transcript
for skill invocations, and return them beside the answer text. Add a skill_loaded grader and one
case, evals/cases/verify-app-loads/case.json. Take only this slice of the invocation battery that
docs/eval-driven-development.html section 11 specifies, and leave the battery for all skills to its
own plan.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the prompt "does this change actually work in the app?" in a fresh session with the plugin
   loaded, when the case runs, then `verify-app` is among the loaded skills in at least 3 of 3 runs.
2. Given the same prompt with no plugin loaded, when the case runs, then the grader reports the skill
   absent rather than failing to parse.
3. Given a transcript holding no skill invocation, when the grader reads it, then it reports a fail
   with the reason, not a crash.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `python3 evals/test_run.py` passes, and covers the new grader.
- The new case passes at least 3 of 3 runs on the with-plugin arm.
- `evals/README.md` names the new grader in its table.

## Out of scope

- The invocation battery for every skill in the plugin. That is its own plan.

title: Let the diagnostician reproduce a bug in a running application
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 2 of `agents/diagnostician.md` is called "Reproduce and Gather Evidence", and its frontmatter
declares four tools: `Read`, `Bash`, `Grep`, and `Glob`. It cannot open the application it is
investigating, so its quality checklist item "The failing behavior was actually reproduced or
observed" cannot be met for a bug in a web page.

## Estimated size

1 file, 50 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Add the browser tools to the frontmatter tool list, and rewrite Step 2 to read the control document
and drive the application when the bug is in a web page. Keep the agent read-only: it gains the
ability to look, never the ability to edit. Require it to say plainly when it could not reach the
application, because a diagnosis built on a guess needs to read as a guess.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a bug in a web page, when the agent investigates, then its Evidence Collected section holds
   an observation it made in the running application.
2. Given a project with no control document, when the agent investigates, then it says it could not
   reach the application and why, rather than reporting a root cause as confirmed.
3. Given the agent's frontmatter, when it is read, then it declares no tool that can change a file.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The frontmatter tool list holds the browser tools, and holds no `Edit` or `Write`.
- Step 2 names the control document and says what to do when it is missing.

title: Add the verify-app-ios skill
description:
## Why (Computational)

A change to a phone screen has the same hole as a change to a web page, and `quality-gates` routes
`mobile-ui` to `/ios-qa` in another plugin. The bead that repoints those rows names a skill that does
not exist yet.

## Estimated size

2 files, 470 LOC, band: Stretch. `skills/ux-audit-ios/SKILL.md` is 479 lines, and this skill covers
the same simulator ground. The registration edits add about 20 more.
design:
Write skills/verify-app-ios/SKILL.md with the same six steps as verify-app, driven by xcrun simctl.
Reuse the capture technique and the Dynamic Type handling already in skills/ux-audit-ios/SKILL.md
rather than inventing a second one. Keep the same machine-readable last line, so quality-gates reads
one result shape for both surfaces. Prove it with a real run rather than by registration alone,

title: Check that every leaf document carries a drive block
description:

description:
## Why (Computational)

These five files govern what the repository does before and during a release: the gates that run,
how a branch lands, how a version is cut, and how agentic code is reviewed. They score 152
violations.

`skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` is the second-worst file in the repository at 70, and it is 911
lines, the longest. It is also the file whose instructions decide whether other work ships, so an
ambiguous sentence in it has the widest blast radius of anything in this phase.

## Estimated size

5 files, about 260 LOC changed, band: Stretch. One file is 911 lines, so the reading is longer than
the diff suggests.

Apply `style-markdown` to these five files, worst first:

| File | Violations | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` | 70 | 911 |
| `docs/adr/0002-the-quality-gates-orchestrator-fans-out-to-blocking-subagents.md` | 31 | 350 |
| `skills/agentic-clean-code/SKILL.md` | 23 | 321 |
| `skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md` | 14 | 555 |
| `skills/ship/SKILL.md` | 14 | 411 |

did not have.

sit inside output templates that an agent fills in and emits. Fixing those changes what a reader
receives at run time, which is the point.

2. Given each file, when searched, then it contains no em-dash and no en-dash.
3. Given `skills/ship/SKILL.md` and `skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md`, when their machine lines and block reason slugs are listed before and after, then the two lists are identical.
4. Given `docs/adr/0002`, when read beside its original, then the decision, its options, and its rationale are unchanged, and nothing was added that the authors did not know at the time.

- All five files carry zero sentences over 30 words, zero metaphors, and zero dashes.

title: Rewrite the repository's Markdown to the style-markdown standard
description:
## Why (Computational)

`style-markdown` shipped in 2.16.0 and governs what gets written next. It says nothing about the
1,160 violations already in the tree, and a rule the tree openly breaks teaches everyone that the
rule is decorative. The em-dash ban is the worked example: it sat in a private config, drifted to
105 occurrences, and `tadw-em-dash-cleanup-mtl` has been open since 2026-08-06.

Measured on 2026-08-27 across 130 tracked Markdown files, excluding `CHANGELOG.md`:

- 112 files carry at least one violation.
- 1,160 violations total: 613 sentences over 30 words, 381 metaphors, 107 dashes, 59 jargon terms.

The stakeholder is every agent that reads these files and executes them. A skill body with a
58-word sentence and an undefined acronym is an instruction the model has to guess at, and the
guess shows up later as behavior nobody asked for.

## Success Criteria

- The three phase beads are closed, and their 16 files carry zero violations.
- A reader can open any of those files and see the standard the repository claims to hold.
- The remaining long tail is smaller than the effort of a fourth phase, so a decision to stop is
  defensible rather than accidental.
design:
Three phases, each one a coherent surface rather than an arbitrary slice, so a reviewer holds one
subject in their head at a time. Phase boundaries follow the feature, not the directory.

The 16 files were chosen by violation density, not by count. Files at 10 or more violations carry
74% of the total; the 16 densest carry 55% in 16% of the files. The long tail of files with one or
two violations is deliberately not scheduled: those cost more in review than they return, and they
get fixed as people touch them.

Each phase is a reading, not a mechanical pass. `style-markdown` says behavior preservation for a
document means it still gives the same instruction, and there is no test to run. So every rule,
path, command, and number that survives an edit must still be true.

Phase order runs densest first, so the highest-value work lands before anyone tires of the effort.

Out of the whole effort: `docs/plans/*`, because a plan is a dated record of what was decided at a
point in time and rewording it falsifies the record. `CHANGELOG.md`, which `.rumdl.toml` already
excludes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `tadw-7xq.1`, `tadw-7xq.2`, and `tadw-7xq.3` are all closed.
- Re-running the violation scan over those 16 files reports zero.
- The full repository check list still passes.

## Out of scope

`docs/plans/*` and `CHANGELOG.md`. The 85 remaining files below 10 violations each, which are left
to opportunistic fixing.

title: Enforce the 100-column wrap on the changed set
description:
## Why (Computational)

The `style-markdown` skill states a 100-column wrap rule, and nothing enforces it. A stated rule
with no check decays exactly as the em-dash ban did, which sat in a private config and drifted to
105 violations inside this repository.

The plan's original approach was to reflow the whole tree first, then enable MD013. Measured, that
cannot ship: MD013 at `line_length = 100`, `code_blocks = false`, `tables = false` reports 1,391
findings across 87 of 123 files, and the largest single file is `skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md` at 129.
There is also no autofix. `rumdl rule MD013` advertises "Fix is always available", but neither
`rumdl fmt` nor `rumdl check --fix` reflows a single line; verified on a copy of
`skills/style-go/SKILL.md`, where both commands left the file byte-identical and all 28 findings
survived.

87 files is past the 30-file hard ceiling for a single bead, and splitting by directory does not
rescue it: `skills/` alone is 38 files.

## Estimated size

3 files, ~40 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Enforce on the changed set instead of the whole tree, so the rule holds from day one and the legacy
tree reflows opportunistically as files are touched.

1. Enable MD013 in `.rumdl.toml` at `line_length = 100`, `code_blocks = false`, `tables = false`,
   replacing the current blanket `disable` entry. Keep the existing comment's reasoning but rewrite
   it to say what is now true. Code blocks and tables stay exempt because wrapping them changes
   meaning, and frontmatter is already skipped by rumdl.
2. In `.githooks/pre-push`, scope the `rumdl check` invocation to the paths
   `skills/quality-gates/scripts/changed_set.py` returns, rather than to `.`. That script already
   resolves the base, compares against the working tree rather than the last commit, and returns
   exit 3 for an unresolvable base as distinct from an empty diff.
3. Keep the whole-tree `rumdl check .` for every rule other than MD013, so the broken-relative-link
   coverage that the em-dash bead adds is not narrowed by this change.

The trade-off, stated plainly: a long prose line in a file nobody touches is never flagged. That is
the point. The alternative is a 1,391-line reflow that the comparable mechanical-cleanup bead,
`tadw-em-dash-cleanup-mtl`, shows is likely to sit open for months.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a changed `.md` file containing a 120-column prose line, when the pre-push hook runs, then it exits non-zero and reports `[MD013]` with that file and line number.
2. Given an untouched `.md` file already carrying lines over 100 columns, when the pre-push hook runs, then it does not fail on that file.
3. Given a changed `.md` file whose only lines over 100 columns are a table row and a line inside a fenced code block, when the pre-push hook runs, then it exits 0.
4. Given `python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py`, when run, then it passes.
5. Given a changed `.md` file containing a broken relative link, when the pre-push hook runs, then it still fails, proving the whole-tree link check was not narrowed to the changed set.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A 120-column prose line in a changed `.md` file fails the pre-push hook, naming file and line.
- The same long line in an untouched file does not fail it.
- A long table row or a long line inside a fenced code block never fails it.
- `python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py` passes.
- The whole-tree link and forbidden-term checks still run and still cover every file.

## Out of scope

Reflowing the existing 87 files. If a full-tree reflow is ever wanted, it needs its own tool bead
plus batched apply beads, because the diff exceeds the hard ceiling by a wide margin.

title: Mechanize the em-dash ban with rumdl MD061
description:
## Why (Computational)

The em-dash and en-dash ban lives in the repository owner's private `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which
ships with nothing, so no plugin consumer ever sees it. Inside this repository it has drifted
anyway: 105 em-dashes across 10 agent, command, and skill files, tracked as
`tadw-em-dash-cleanup-mtl`. Some sit inside output templates that an agent fills in and emits, so
the rule is being broken at runtime in documents handed to a reader.

Writing the rule into a skill makes it travel. Only the linter makes it hold.

A second hole rides along and is worth closing in the same change. CI runs `rumdl fmt --check .`,
which is the formatter, not the linter. Verified: a document containing a broken relative link and a
non-descriptive link label passes `rumdl fmt --check` with exit 0, while `rumdl check` exits 1 and
names both. `check_doc_paths.py` defaults to README, AGENTS, and CLAUDE only, and its verdict is
WARN by design. So today a broken relative link anywhere under `skills/` is caught by nothing.

## Estimated size

4 files, ~30 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Use the linter this repository already runs rather than writing a new guard script.

1. Bump `RUMDL_VERSION` in `.github/workflows/lint.yml` line 17 from `v0.2.18` to `v0.2.33`, the
   version MD061 was verified on. This replaces the question of whether the older pin carries the
   rule.
2. Add `[MD061] terms` for the em-dash and en-dash to `.rumdl.toml`, with a comment naming the rule
   and its blind spot. Verified behavior: MD061 skips fenced code blocks, inline code spans, and
   YAML frontmatter. The fence and code-span behavior is exactly right, because code samples and
   quoted external text must keep their punctuation. The frontmatter skip is a real gap covering
   three of the 105 occurrences, and it is documented rather than worked around.
3. Add `rumdl check .` to the `AGENTS.md` check list and to `.githooks/pre-push`, and update the
   stated pre-push count from 14 to 15.

Why not a `check_markdown_style.py`. The one invariant with proven drift is already expressible as a
rumdl rule. `style-testing` earned its checker for an invariant no linter can express, namely "no
framework token in the body with one delimited appendix exempt". `check_doc_paths.py` already covers
path claims, and its own header records that a prose gate reported 194 misses with zero real. Every
new suite is a permanent tax on every push, and the hook already runs 14 checks in tens of seconds.

Fallback if `tadw-em-dash-cleanup-mtl` stalls: land `rumdl check .` without the MD061 terms. That
closes the broken-link hole immediately at zero cost, and the MD061 line becomes a one-line
follow-up on the cleanup bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a tracked `.md` file with an em-dash added to a prose sentence, when `rumdl check .` runs, then it exits 1 and reports `[MD061]` with that file and line number.
2. Given the same em-dash placed inside a fenced code block, when `rumdl check .` runs, then it exits 0.
3. Given the same em-dash placed in a YAML frontmatter value, when `rumdl check .` runs, then it exits 0, and `.rumdl.toml` carries a comment recording that this is a known limit.
4. Given `python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py`, when run after `rumdl check .` is added to the hook, then it passes and the hook's success line reports 15 checks rather than 14.
5. Given `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, when read, then `RUMDL_VERSION` is `v0.2.33`.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `rumdl check .` exits 0 on a clean tree.
- It exits 1, naming file and line, when an em-dash is added to prose in any tracked `.md` file.
- It exits 0 when that same em-dash sits inside a fenced code block.
- `python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py` passes with the new check counted.
- The CI Markdown job installs `v0.2.33`.

## Out of scope

Removing the 105 existing em-dashes. That is `tadw-em-dash-cleanup-mtl`, which blocks this bead and
is not absorbed by it. The frontmatter blind spot is documented, not fixed; three occurrences do not
justify a bespoke scanner.

title: Spell bd export with -o everywhere an agent might execute it
description:
`bd export` with no `-o` writes the JSONL to stdout. It exits 0 and touches nothing, so a bare `bd export` is a silent no-op against .beads/issues.jsonl. Nothing errors, the tracker looks healthy, and the export goes stale while bv and Manifest keep reading the old file.

I hit this in-session on 2026-08-26: I ran `bd export >/dev/null 2>&1` after creating tadw-9ff, reported the tracker exported, and the bead was absent from .beads/issues.jsonl. The redirect sent the entire export to /dev/null.

Audit result across this repo: every place that tells an agent to EXECUTE the command already uses the correct `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`. That covers commands/plan-to-beads.md, commands/bead-refine.md, skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md, skills/bead-create/SKILL.md:244, skills/ship/SKILL.md, skills/roadmap-dashboard/, agents/project-manager.md, docs/beads-workflow.md, and both hook scripts.

What is left is bare-prose mentions that an agent could act on:

- skills/bead-create/SKILL.md:270 'Run `bd export` yourself, and mention it only on failure'
- skills/bead-create/SKILL.md:282 'Ask the author to run `bd export`'
- skills/bead-create/SKILL.md:302 checklist: '`bd export` ran, and was reported only if it failed'
- AGENTS.md:398 'Never ask the author to run `bd export`'

Line 244 of that skill gives the right form, so an agent reading top to bottom is fine. An agent that jumps to the line-302 checklist sees only the bare form. That is the exact path that failed for me.

Also prose, and lower risk because they describe ship's conflict resolution rather than instruct: README.md:191, docs/ROUTING.md:260, skills/publish-plugin/SKILL.md:194.

Reported by the atlas-ae session, which confirmed atlas's own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md already use the -o form.
design:
Two options.

A. Spell the flag everywhere, including prose. Cheapest, and it removes the trap wherever a reader lands. Costs a little readability in sentences that are about the step rather than the command.

B. Leave prose bare and add one line to docs/beads-workflow.md saying the bare form writes to stdout. Keeps the prose clean, but relies on the reader having read that page.

Prefer A for the four instructional sites above, since bead-create's checklist is written to be jumped to. B alone does not fix that path.

Do not add a wrapper or an alias. The flag is the fix.
acceptance_criteria:
- The four sites listed in the description name the file: `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`.
- docs/beads-workflow.md states that a bare `bd export` writes to stdout and updates no file.
- `grep -rn 'bd export' --include='*.md' .` shows no remaining instruction to execute the bare form; prose describing the step may keep it.
- python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py still passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Log the two silent marker-discard paths in handle_stop
description:
handle_stop in scripts/label_bead_on_skill_invocation.sh throws away a malformed marker without writing a bead-label.log line. Two paths do this:

1. Line ~775, the no-separator path: the filename carries no "__", so no label prefix can be read. It calls log() (stderr) and then rm -f, with no log_outcome call.
2. Line ~788, the malformed-header path: `created` is not all digits, or `bead_id` is empty. It calls rm -f with no log() and no log_outcome, so it leaves no trace at all.

The stale-TTL path directly below them does call log_outcome, so the shape to copy is already in the file.

This matters because bead-label.log exists precisely because stderr goes unread in a hook. A marker discarded on either path is a label that never got applied, and today nothing durable records that.

Found by the meridian session on 2026-08-26 while exercising handle_stop with a non-numeric timestamp, a past-TTL marker, and a filename with no "__" separator. All three exited 0, so the set -u arithmetic trap stays closed. Only the logging is missing.
design: log_outcome takes: event, skill, branch, bead_id, message. On the no-separator path, bead_id has not been read yet; read line 2 of the marker inline, and pass the unresolved default when it is empty. On the malformed-header path, both `created` and `bead_id` may be junk; pass what is there and say which field failed.
acceptance_criteria:
- The no-separator discard writes one bead-label.log line naming the discarded filename.
- The malformed-header discard writes one bead-label.log line saying which field failed validation.
- Both paths still exit 0 and still rm -f the marker.
- A test in hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh covers each path and asserts the log line.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cover the 12 uncovered commands in docs/ROUTING.md
description:
docs/ROUTING.md claims to be the long form of the AGENTS.md routing table, but it has sections for only 18 of the 30 commands. title: Installer rewrites settings.json for cosmetic jq differences alone
description:
Found reinstalling into atlas on 2026-08-23. --check reported 'all three events reference the hook', and the install that followed still reported 'wired' rather than 'already wired' and wrote a settings.json.bak file.

The diff was entirely cosmetic: jq rewrote a \u003e escape back to a literal >, and added a trailing newline the file lacked. No hook entry changed.

The cause is that the installer compares the jq OUTPUT against the original bytes. jq normalizes escaping and whitespace on any round trip, so a settings.json that was not written by jq differs from its own re-serialization even when nothing semantic changed. The result is a spurious backup file, an untracked file left in the target repository, and a 'wired' report that overstates what happened.

Pre-existing behavior, not introduced by tadw-44y, but tadw-44y made it visible by adding --check next to it: the two now disagree about whether anything needs doing.
design: Compare semantically rather than byte-wise. Run the ORIGINAL through jq with an identity filter and compare that normalized form against the patched output, so only a real change counts as a change. Keep writing the backup when a real change happens.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Installing into a repository whose settings.json is already correctly wired but not jq-formatted reports 'already wired' and writes no backup.
2. A real wiring change still reports 'wired' and still writes a backup first.
3. hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh covers both, and passes.

title: /tadw:ship deletes the worktree the calling session lives in
description:
skills/ship/SKILL.md Step 5 removes the worktree holding the shipped branch, and the skill says outright that it 'is usually invoked from inside the very worktree it is about to delete' (skills/ship/SKILL.md:468-470). The session survives the removal, so $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR then names a directory that is gone.

This is the mechanism that produced tadw-1rf. That bead guarded the hook command strings, so the state is now quiet instead of an error on every turn. Quiet is not working: a session in a deleted directory labels no bead and writes no log line, because the script that writes the log is the missing file. The user is told nothing.

Found by the altitude arm of /simplify on 2026-08-23, reviewing the tadw-1rf diff.
design:
The guard in tadw-1rf sits at the wrong end of the problem on purpose, because a hook cannot see its own project directory disappear. The deeper fix is at the layer that does the deleting.

Options, cheapest first:
  1. Say it in the skill. Step 5 already carries a 'leave the worktree before removing it' rule; add that a session still open in it keeps running and stops labeling, so the operator should end that session. Documentation only, no detection.
  2. Detect and warn. Before 'git worktree remove', look for a live process whose cwd is the worktree. What worked by hand: pgrep -f 'dangerously-skip-permissions', then lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd -Fn for each. Report the pid and let the operator decide, since killing somebody's session unasked is worse than the stale state.
  3. Refuse. Too strong: /tadw:ship runs unattended, and the session it would refuse for is usually its own caller.

Option 1 plus 2 as a warning looks right. Do not kill any process.
acceptance_criteria:
1. /tadw:ship names the consequence before removing a worktree: a session left open there labels nothing.
2. When a live process has the worktree as its working directory, the removal step reports the pid rather than removing silently.
3. The step still completes unattended, and it kills nothing.
4. It never warns about a worktree no process occupies.
5. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh and python3 .githooks/test_prepush.py both still pass.
close_reason: shipped: warn before removing a worktree a session still stands in (5d62cc8)

title: Bead-label hook: a <bead-id>-<slug> branch resolves nothing
description:
Found while dogfooding tadw-b14 on 2026-08-22. Branch tadw-b14-hook-resolution-and-clean-tree resolves to no bead, and --doctor says so plainly.

The cause is that resolve_bead's pattern matches maximal hyphenated runs, so the whole branch name comes out as one token and the tadw-b14 prefix inside it is never offered as a candidate. Renaming the branch to the outrigger shape (outrigger/tadw-b14/<slug>) made it resolve at once, because the positional rule reads segment two.

This is pre-existing, not a regression from tadw-b14: the older pattern took the same maximal run.

CORRECTED 2026-08-24. This bead originally claimed close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh already decomposes prefixes this way, and that is false. Its BEAD_ID_RE at close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh:198 takes the same maximal hyphenated run, so it is blind to this branch shape too. The "longest candidate first" comment beside it describes sort order, not decomposition. Verified by reading the regex and running it against the branch name. So there was no decomposition to port, and this fix writes one in the label hook.

The close hook is NOT worth fixing for this, which is why no follow-up bead was filed. It reads four sources in order at close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh:275 (title, branchref, body, commits), so a branchref that yields no known id falls through instead of ending the run. In this repository the fallback is what fires: squash-merge headlines end in (tadw-44y)-style parens and the regex extracts the bare id from those. There are also no PRs here, since /tadw:ship squash-merges locally and closes the bead itself. Porting prefix candidates there would create new ways to trip the deliberate ambiguity refusal at :280, turning a working close into a refusal.

Cost: anyone naming a branch <bead-id>-<slug>, which is a common convention, gets no labels and no warning beyond a log line.
design:
Offer hyphen-separated PREFIXES of a candidate as further candidates, shortest-plausible last. The MAX_BEAD_PROBES cap already bounds the added cost.

CORRECTED 2026-08-24. This field originally said to take the decomposition from close_bead_on_pr_merge.sh rather than writing a second one, on the ground that the two hooks disagreed about the same branch. The close hook has no such decomposition; see the description. Both hooks were blind to this branch shape in the same way, so the decomposition was written here.

The invariant that instruction was protecting still holds, and it is the one to preserve: a slug-shaped id such as tadw-qg-prepush-verdict-gate-tug must match whole before tadw-qg is tried. Emitting the full token first, and keeping it the longest, gives the existing tier/length sort that ordering for free. A dotted epic-child suffix is never split off, since hdw-3fe4.3 and hdw-3fe4 are different beads.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Branch tadw-b14-hook-resolution-and-clean-tree resolves to tadw-b14.
2. The positional segment still wins over any prefix, so the existing ordering case still passes.
3. The probe cap still holds: a branch offering more tokens than the cap issues no more than MAX_BEAD_PROBES bd show calls.
4. bash hooks/test-claude-scripts.sh passes with zero failures.
close_reason: shipped: fix: resolve a bead-id-slug branch in the label hook (tadw-51e)

title: Bead-label hook: account for inject-mode labels, and record why ship is unmapped
description:
inject mode can drop a label with no trace. gate mode writes a marker with a TTL and resolves it at Stop; the inject arm of run_label_flow emits an instruction and keeps no state. In the 2026-08-22 fathom session /tadw:verify-acceptance reached ACCEPTED, which clears its gate, and no accepted label was applied. Nothing recorded that one had been owed.

Separately, skill_for_command has no ship entry and neither does classify_skill: the string 'ship' appears nowhere in the script. That is the right call, because /tadw:ship closes the bead outright and a label applied at that moment carries no information the closed state does not. It is currently indistinguishable from an oversight.

Plan: docs/plans/bead-label-hook-resolution-and-visibility.md, M5. Depends on tadw-qjj for the log this leans on.
design:
1. inject mode writes a marker alongside gate's, distinguished by mode. handle_stop reads it, applies no label, and logs when a requested inject label never appeared. Reuse MARKER_TTL_SECONDS.

2. Add a comment to skill_for_command recording that ship and tadw:ship are deliberately unmapped because /tadw:ship closes the bead. No entry, no label.

title: Step 3 re-runs changed_set.py, so the base can differ from Step 2's
description:
## Why (Computational)

skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md Step 3's documented pipeline calls changed_set.py a second time and pipes it into route_qa.py:

    python3 .../changed_set.py --repo-root . | python3 .../route_qa.py --repo-root . --paths-from - --base "$BASE"

Step 4's lane-input table now states the base SHA and the changed path list come from 'Step 2's changed_set.py, run exactly once', and Gate 7 states what a second resolution costs: two runs against a moving working tree can disagree, and the report's Scope line would then name one base while a gate counted against another. The report would still read clean.

The wall-clock cost is small (one git diff plus one ls-files). The correctness cost is the one the fan-out design spends a whole coupling on, so the procedure currently contradicts its own rule in the default path.

Found by the /simplify efficiency pass over commit a814d94.
design:
Step 2 writes its stdout to a file inside the git directory, beside the probe spec and the report artifact, which is where this skill already puts per-run scratch:

    python3 .../changed_set.py --repo-root . > "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/quality-gates-changed.txt"

Step 3 then reads that file rather than re-running the script:

    python3 .../route_qa.py --repo-root . --paths-from "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/quality-gates-changed.txt" --base "$BASE"

route_qa.py already accepts --paths-from FILE, so no script changes. The prose at SKILL.md that explains why Step 2 puts paths on stdout and everything else on stderr needs rewording, since the pipe is what it justifies.

Check whether .githooks/pre-push or any other caller reproduces the two-command pipe before changing it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given Step 2 has run, when Step 3 runs, then changed_set.py has been invoked exactly once for the whole run.
2. Given the Step 3 code block in SKILL.md, when read, then it takes its paths from the file Step 2 wrote rather than from a second changed_set.py invocation.
3. Given the prose that justifies stdout-versus-stderr separation, when read after the change, then it describes the shape the skill actually uses.
4. Given the repository check suite, when run, then all 13 suites pass, including test_route_qa.py and test_changed_set.py.

title: Name one authoritative ruler for the triage-beads effort tier
description:
## Why (Computational)

The ROI rubric in `skills/triage-beads/SKILL.md` picks the effort tier with four different measures,
and they disagree. "Effort: the divisor" lists `estimated_minutes` with cut points at 30 and 120
minutes, then a `plan-to-beads` size band counted in files and lines, then `bv`'s "Low complexity"
flag, then a count of acceptance criteria.

A change of one file and 100 lines is small by the second measure and is rarely under 30 minutes by
the first. So two people pricing the same bead pick different tiers. Effort divides the score, so it
moves the result more than any single value point does, and it is stored on only 1 of the 14 open
beads.

The stakeholder is anyone who reads the rubric to argue with a pick. That is the whole reason the ROI
rewrite in `ee3f6cf` exists.

## Estimated size

1 file, about 15 lines changed, band: below Target. Documentation only. No script and no test in this
repository reads these numbers.
design:
Name minutes the authoritative measure, because `estimated_minutes` is a stored field, and express the
other three as mappings onto it rather than as tiers of their own.

Then re-derive every number the skill prints, the way `ee3f6cf` did. The sample leaderboard shows its
own arithmetic, and a stale number there is worse than having no example.

Shrunk by /bead-refine on 2026-08-24. Two of the three original items are removed. Both were true and
neither could change an answer:

- The value heading advertises 0 to 23 points while a ready P0 wins by override before any arithmetic
  runs. A reader can misjudge the range. No pick moves.
- The unblock cap of 6 needs a bead that releases three others, and the most any open bead releases is
  1. The cap never binds.

The bead's own text said none of the three changes a ranking. That is true of those two. It is not
true of the effort measures, which change the tier and therefore the divisor.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the "Effort: the divisor" section, when read, then exactly one measure is named authoritative and the other three are expressed as mappings onto it.
2. Given a bead of one file and 100 changed lines with no stored minutes, when two readers apply the section, then both reach the same tier.
3. Given every ROI number printed in the skill, when each is recomputed from its own stated parts, then it matches to one decimal place.
4. Given `rumdl fmt --check .`, when run, then it exits 0.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- One measure is named authoritative in "Effort: the divisor", and the other three map onto it
- Every ROI number the skill prints is recomputed and matches its own stated parts

## Out of scope

- The advertised value range of 0 to 23, and the unblock cap of 6. Both were removed from this bead
  because neither can change a pick.

title: Cover the untested-change and planted-secret findings with fixture evals
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2 and Gate 6 are the two gates most likely to be quietly weakened, since one is
judgment and the other is a pattern list. Nothing currently checks that the skill reports a
finding when a real defect is present, only that it reports nothing when the tree is clean.

The stakeholder is anyone who trusts a clean report on a repository that has an untested branch
or a committed key.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

5 files, about 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two fixture repositories and two single-arm cases.

`gates-untested-change` plants a new function with a branch and no test anywhere. It asserts the
change-coverage gate reports FAIL with the case enumerated, not merely that something failed.

`gates-planted-secret` plants a fake `AKIA` key in a source file. It asserts the secrets gate
reports FAIL with a `file:line`, and, critically, that the key's value appears nowhere in the
report.

That last assertion mirrors at the report level the rule `test_check_secrets.py` pins at the
script level. Checking it in both places means a leak is caught wherever it is introduced,
whether in the script's output or in the skill's prose about how to render a finding.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the `gates-untested-change` fixture, when the case runs, then the report grades change coverage FAIL and enumerates the untested case.
2. Given the `gates-planted-secret` fixture, when the case runs, then the report shows a secrets FAIL with a `file:line`.
3. Given the same run, when scanning the whole report text, then the planted key's value does not appear.
4. Given three runs of each case, when the suite finishes, then all three pass for each.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `gates-untested-change` and `gates-planted-secret` exist with their fixtures
- Each passes three runs out of three
- The planted-secret case asserts the key's value is absent from the report

title: Release 2.6.0
description:
## Why (Computational)

Everything else in this plan is inert for anyone consuming the plugin from the
marketplace rather than from `main`.

The stakeholder is the plugin's users, who get none of the hardening until a version is tagged
and published.

This bead needs a person: tagging and pushing a release is outward-facing and should not be
settled by an agent alone.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M7)

machinery, all backward compatible with existing invocations.

Write a Keep a Changelog `## [2.6.0]` section above `## [2.5.2]`, moving anything under
`## [Unreleased]` into it. Match the existing entries' voice: each bullet leads with a bolded
sentence saying what changed and why it mattered, not a bare feature name.

Update both link-reference lines at the foot of `CHANGELOG.md`: point `[Unreleased]` at
`v2.6.0...HEAD`, and add a `[2.6.0]` line comparing `v2.5.2...v2.6.0`.

Tag last, so `.githooks/reference-transaction` validates the manifest before anything is

1. Given `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, when reading `version`, then it is 2.6.0.
2. Given `CHANGELOG.md`, when reading the 2.6.0 section, then every script, hook, artifact, and eval addition from this plan appears.

## Out of scope

Any code change. This bead ships what the other beads built; if it uncovers a defect, that is a
new bead, not a fix folded in here.

title: Make the prompt-assets shape checkable
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2's shape table asks the model to confirm a prompt asset "parses, is registered
where the project says, and its embedded commands are valid" without naming a single command, so
the grade is pure judgment.

This repository is the primary consumer of that row, since nearly every change here is a prompt
asset. The stakeholder is anyone whose skill shipped undiscoverable, which is what happened in
2.4.1: a `bead-audit` frontmatter scalar containing "verdicts: content" ended early, the
frontmatter failed to parse, and both name and description were dropped at load time.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M5)

## Estimated size

1 file, about 55 LOC changed, band: Target.
design:
Replace the vague cell with four items, each naming a command or a grep. The row points at a short
subsection below the table, because a table cell cannot hold a checklist.

1. `claude plugin validate .` passes, so the frontmatter parses. Keep this item even though
   `.githooks/reference-transaction` already gates it: that hook fires only when a `v*` tag is
   created, and `.githooks/pre-push:42` records that the push deliberately skips it. So nothing
   checks frontmatter between releases, which is exactly when a skill ships undiscoverable.
2. Some agent or command references the skill, or it is a documented accepted orphan (the
   `business-ideas` and `idea-wizard` precedent).
3. Every command embedded in the asset is valid: scripts it names exist at the stated paths, and
   flags it shows match the script's argparse. `hooks/test-hooks.js` already parses every bash block
   with `bash -n`, so this item covers only what that misses: path existence and flag agreement.
   `skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py:50` limits itself to `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
   and `CLAUDE.md`, so a path named inside a `SKILL.md` is checked by nothing today.
4. Where the repository has an eval harness, a change to behavior-bearing prose carries an eval
   case, and its absence is a WARN naming the harness.

State in the subsection that a script is not a component, so the registration question is N/A for
one. Without that line the next reader reports a false gap on every script this plan adds.

Shrunk by /bead-refine on 2026-08-24. The original fifth item, "the component is registered in the
`AGENTS.md` name list and the `README.md` description table", is removed because
`hooks/test-hooks.js:492` already asserts it mechanically for skills, agents, and commands, with
matching counts. A checklist item that duplicates a passing test costs a reader's attention and
buys nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the subsection, when reading each of the four items, then each names a command or grep a second person could run without asking the author.
2. Given a new script with no component registration, when the checklist is applied, then the registration question is N/A by a stated rule rather than a failure.
3. Given the subsection, when read against `hooks/test-hooks.js`, then no item restates a check that suite already makes.
